# Herdr downtime dispatcher: scheduled prompts (best-effort frequency)

## Problem statement

The Herdr downtime dispatcher only ever dispatches worklog-derived work (audit → implement → plan → intake tiers). There is no mechanism for periodic, project-scoped prompts (e.g. `/skill:refactor`) to run during downtime on a best-effort cadence, so recurring maintenance must be triggered manually.

## Users

- Operators running the Herdr downtime worker who want recurring maintenance prompts executed automatically during local-LLM idle time.

### User stories

- As an operator, I want `/skill:refactor` to run automatically at least every three days during downtime so the codebase stays clean without manual intervention.
- As an operator, I want scheduled prompts stored in a config file carrying each prompt's desired frequency and last-triggered datetime so I can add, remove, or adjust entries without code changes.
- As an operator, I want a scheduled prompt to dispatch only when the downtime dispatcher actually has a free LLM slot, so maintenance never interrupts active work.
- As an operator, I want scheduled prompts held during a code freeze so no new code changes land mid-release.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl init` provisions a project-local config file `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` containing the base set of scheduled commands — starting with a single `/skill:refactor` entry (`intervalDays: 3`, `lastTriggeredAt: null`) — via a default config template (e.g. `templates/scheduled-prompts.json`). Provisioning is create-if-absent: re-running `wl init` never clobbers an existing file (user edits and `lastTriggeredAt` state are preserved).
2. The config file holds a list of scheduled prompts; each entry has a stable id, the prompt text (any text the pi agent pane can run, e.g. `/skill:refactor`), a best-effort frequency in days (`intervalDays`), and `lastTriggeredAt` (ISO-8601 UTC datetime; `null` = never run). When the file is absent (e.g. a worklog root created before this feature) the worker treats the set as empty: no scheduled dispatch, a logged notice, and existing tiers unaffected (fail-closed; `wl init` is the provisioning path). Malformed files also fail closed: no scheduled dispatch, error logged, existing tiers unaffected.
3. The downtime dispatch pipeline checks scheduled prompts FIRST (before the audit/implement/plan/intake tiers): when an LLM slot is idle and the threshold is met, an entry is due iff `lastTriggeredAt` is null or `now - lastTriggeredAt >= intervalDays` (best effort — a delayed dispatch never fires more often than the frequency). A due entry dispatches a pi agent pane through the existing spawn path (`send-to-pi.sh`, `--pane-name Downtime <id>`, `--no-focus`, `--cwd <wlRoot>`, `--model <downtimeModel>`) running the prompt text.
4. On successful spawn of a scheduled prompt: `lastTriggeredAt` is updated to `now` and persisted to the config file (atomic tmp+rename write), and the dispatch is recorded in `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` with kind `scheduled` (no work-item comment/claim — there is no item). Fail-closed: if the config update or the log-marker write fails, the spawn ABORTS (an unrecorded dispatch never runs) and the entry remains due for the next idle slot.
5. Code-freeze gate applies to scheduled prompts exactly as to the audit/implement tiers: while the marker is frozen or ambiguous (fail-closed), scheduled prompts are skipped and dispatch falls through to the plan/intake tiers (unchanged existing behaviour).
6. When no scheduled prompt is due, the existing tier pipeline runs unchanged (audit → implement → plan → intake). A due scheduled prompt dispatches instead of reaching the backlog tiers, so it never triggers the no-candidate cooldown; when no prompt is due and the backlog is genuinely empty, the existing no-candidate cooldown applies unchanged.
7. Config entries with invalid `intervalDays` (missing, non-finite, or ≤ 0) or missing/empty prompt text are skipped with a logged warning (fail-closed, never a crash); entries missing `lastTriggeredAt` are treated as due. When multiple entries are due, they dispatch one per idle slot in config order.
8. Unit/integration tests cover: `wl init` provisioning (file created with the base set on first init; untouched on re-init), due-check arithmetic (null lastTriggeredAt, boundary, not-yet-due), config parse/defaults/atomic-write, absent/malformed-config fail-closed, freeze gating, cooldown interaction, spawn args, and the `scheduled` log-marker record.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (e.g. `packages/herdr/README.md`, `PLUGIN_GUIDE.md`, `CONFIG.md` downtime sections).
10. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Follow the worker's existing fail-closed philosophy at every boundary: never dispatch, never throw.
- Scheduled check is the first tier of `dispatchDowntimeWork`, gated by the same fresh-read code-freeze marker as audit/implement.
- Per-process single-flight guard (`dispatchInFlight`) applies to scheduled dispatch too — one dispatch per idle slot.
- Reuse the existing scheduler-loop wiring (`createDowntimeWorker.tick`); no new timer infrastructure.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchDowntimeWork` tier pipeline (freeze gate → audit → implement → plan → intake), `buildDowntimePrompt`/`buildDowntimePaneArgs`, `DowntimeWorkerDeps` injectable boundary, no-candidate cooldown + three-strike rule in `createDowntimeWorker.tick`, settings clamps.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — wires deps (`getNextItem`, `getNextAuditCandidate`, `getNextImplementCandidate`, `readCodeFreezeStatus`, `claimItem`, `spawnAgentPane`, `recordDispatch`, `recordError`).
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — JSON-file settings store pattern (`~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`), defaults-merge + clamp pattern to mirror.
- `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` — rolling dispatch markers (kind `plan|intake|audit|implement`).
- Code-freeze marker: `.worklog/code-freeze.json` (WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY).

## Desired change

Add a scheduled-prompts tier as the first dispatch stage, provisioned by `wl init`. CLI side: `src/commands/init.ts` copies a default config template (new `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` with the `/skill:refactor` base set) into `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` when absent (create-if-absent, never clobber). Plugin side: new module `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` (config load/save/due-check, mirroring `settings.ts` patterns); extend `DowntimeWorkerDeps` with `getDueScheduledPrompt(cwd)` (or equivalent) and reuse `recordDispatch` with kind `scheduled` + a `ScheduledPrompt` event shape; add `dispatchScheduledPrompt` beside `dispatchClaimedTier` (update+persist lastTriggeredAt → log-marker → spawn, abort before spawn on failure); insert the tier in `dispatchDowntimeWork` under the freeze gate. Wire the fs-backed deps in `index.ts`.

## Key Files

- `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (new) — default config template: base set with the `/skill:refactor` entry (`intervalDays: 3`, `lastTriggeredAt: null`).
- `src/commands/init.ts` — provision `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` from the template, create-if-absent (never clobber); `src/commands/init.test.ts` (or existing init tests) for provisioning + no-clobber.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` (new) — config schema, load (absent ⇒ empty set, fail-closed), atomic save, due-check (`isDueScheduledPrompt` / `getDueScheduledPrompt`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `ScheduledPrompt` types, `DowntimeDispatchEvent`/`DowntimeDispatchOutcome` kind `scheduled`, `dispatchScheduledPrompt`, tier insertion in `dispatchDowntimeWork`, deps additions.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — wire fs-backed scheduled-prompt deps (read config, persist lastTriggeredAt, rolling-log record).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` (+ new `scheduled-prompts.test.ts`) — due-check, config, freeze, cooldown, spawn-arg, log-marker tests.
- `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` — runtime per-worklog-root config (created by `wl init`, then updated in place by the worker; not committed).
- Docs: `packages/herdr/README.md`, `PLUGIN_GUIDE.md`, `CONFIG.md` — document the config file, `wl init` provisioning, frequency semantics, and freeze behaviour.

## Related work

- WL-0MRHYQU1S009DJ9B — *Add periodic request scheduling to pi worklog plugin* (completed): cron-based scheduling in the pi extension (`ctx.isIdle()` + `pi.sendUserMessage()`); related pattern, different plugin — reuse the "any prompt text" lesson, not the cron model.
- WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K — *Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime*: parent of the downtime worker.
- WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY — code-freeze gate (freeze semantics reused here).
- WL-0MSI7DQL10016QYX — no-candidate cooldown (interaction confirmed in AC5).
- WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6 — implement tier (tier ordering).
- WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8 — dispatch logging (rolling `.worklog` log + item comments; `scheduled` entries are log-only).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the provisioning path for the config file is `wl init` (the standard worklog-root setup command); the plugin treats an absent file as an empty set (fail-closed, logged) rather than synthesizing defaults.
- **Assumption:** frequency granularity is whole days (`intervalDays`); "every three days" = 72 h. Best-effort means a dispatch may be delayed (no idle slot, cooldown, freeze) but never happens more often than the frequency.
- **Assumption:** multiple due entries dispatch one per idle slot in config order; the single-flight guard prevents overlap.
- **Risk:** concurrent user edit vs worker write of the config file (last-writer-wins) — mitigated by atomic tmp+rename writes and re-reading before each persist.
- **Risk:** clock skew/stale `lastTriggeredAt` makes an entry appear immediately due — acceptable (best-effort), documented.
- **Risk:** `/skill:refactor` runs while the operator is actively working — mitigated: dispatch only happens when an LLM slot is actually idle for the full threshold, unchanged from existing behaviour.
- **Scope creep:** cron-style schedules, per-prompt model overrides, TUI editing of prompts, per-project prompt defaults beyond refactor — record as separate linked work items, not this scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Where should the scheduled-prompts config file live?" — Answer (user/rgardler): "as recommended" — project-local `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, scoping prompts per worklog root (the dispatcher's `cwd`). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "During a code freeze (ship-it marker), should due scheduled prompts still dispatch?" — Answer (user/rgardler): "not during a code-freeze" — scheduled prompts are held by the same freeze gate as the audit/implement tiers (frozen OR ambiguous ⇒ skip; plan/intake still run). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Should a due scheduled prompt bypass the empty-backlog no-candidate cooldown?" — Answer (user/rgardler): "confirmed" — the scheduled check is the first dispatch tier, so a due prompt dispatches instead of reaching the backlog tiers and never triggers the cooldown; when none are due, existing backlog + cooldown behaviour is unchanged. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Requirement (user/rgardler, mid-draft directive): "Add a requirement that wl init will add a base set of scheduled commands, starting with just /skill:refactor (provide a default config file for this purpose)" — Answer: accepted verbatim; `wl init` provisions `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` from a `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` default (base set = `/skill:refactor`, `intervalDays: 3`, `lastTriggeredAt: null`), create-if-absent, never clobbering user edits or `lastTriggeredAt` state. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
data.title: Herdr downtime dispatcher: scheduled prompts (best-effort frequency) config

# Tests: inline-note edit & persistence

## Summary
Automated coverage for the interactive inline-note editing feature: marker add/edit/delete, surgical write-back with byte-level preservation, paragraph↔marker mapping, local placeholder id stability, viewer cursor mapping, and the podcast note-child lifecycle — for both `.podcast.md` scripts and generic markdown documents.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Marker-edit helpers: insert/update/remove `[NOTE <id>: ...]` markers (including `DONE` variants, PRD §7.1/§7.3) on paragraphs with and without an existing marker — podcast and generic markdown.
- [ ] Byte-preservation: after an edit/delete, all file content outside the edited paragraph is preserved byte-for-byte.
- [ ] Paragraph↔marker mapping: a marker is correctly located in a multi-paragraph document; the selected paragraph's marker (if any) is returned.
- [ ] Local placeholder ids: the `LOCAL-<seq>` scheme is deterministic for unchanged documents (stable across re-opens).
- [ ] Viewer cursor mapping: rendered viewer line ↔ source paragraph/block mapping is covered.
- [ ] Note-child sync (podcast): add → `wl create --parent <episode>`; delete/resolve → `DONE` marker + resolution comment on the child — tested with a mocked `wl` CLI. Unresolvable episode → prominent warning emitted, no silent skip.
- [ ] All new tests pass via `npx vitest run packages/herdr`; the full project test suite passes once WL-0MSNSZ4R6009AU0N (herdr build fix) is resolved.

## Minimal Implementation
- Extend `packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.test.ts` and add `packages/herdr/src/md-note-edit.test.ts` for the new pure helpers (TDD red/green with the implementation features).
- New viewer-integration tests in `worklist.test.ts`: cursor selection, chord wiring, write-back — with dependency-injected file reader/writer.

# Intake Draft: Downtime dispatcher — priority-first selection with round-robin tie-break across tied items + jittered probes

## Problem statement

When multiple instances of the herdr plugin are active on the same machine, the same instance often wins the race to dispatch in downtime — with a deterministic ascending-sortIndex tie-break, the same lowest-sortIndex item is always picked first by whichever instance is fastest, so one instance monopolises dispatch and tied-priority items are never rotated. Probes also fire in lockstep (all instances at the same fixed poll interval), which amplifies the same-winner effect and gives other machines no chance to get into the loop.

## Users

- **Operator with several herdr panes/instances on one machine** — wants the downtime work spread fairly: highest-priority items first, tied-priority items rotated round-robin, and no single instance hogs all dispatches.
- **Operator with multiple machines sharing the llama proxy** — wants probes desynchronised so each machine gets a fair chance to dispatch first.

### User stories

- As an operator running N herdr instances on one machine, when multiple candidates tie on priority, I want them dispatched in round-robin rotation (shared across instances) so no single item/instance dominates.
- As an operator with several machines on the proxy, I want each downtime probe delayed by a random amount (within ±50% of the poll interval) so instances do not probe in lockstep and other machines can win the dispatch race.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Priority-first selection is preserved: a higher-priority candidate is always selected before any lower-priority candidate, regardless of round-robin state (all tiers: audit, implement, plan/intake).
- [ ] Round-robin tie-break: among candidates sharing the same priority level, selection rotates through them using a shared, durable cursor persisted under `<cwd>/.worklog/` (e.g. `downtime-round-robin.json`), so repeated dispatches of a tied group do not always pick the same item; two instances selecting from the same group pick different items when the cursor has advanced. Unit tests cover rotation across repeated selections and across the three tier selectors.
- [ ] Shared state is fail-open and never blocks dispatch: a missing, unreadable, or corrupt round-robin file degrades to default (no rotation) behaviour; the cursor write failure is tolerated (marker/log write ordering unchanged — the dispatched-marker remains the authoritative guard against re-dispatch).
- [ ] Probe jitter: the downtime task's effective poll interval is jittered ±50% of the configured `downtimePollIntervalMs` per tick (random, injectable RNG for deterministic tests); two workers with identical configuration do not probe in lockstep. Jitter range is verified by unit tests (min/max bounds).
- [ ] Absorbs WL-0MSMHX6IR007F3H6 (Stagger herdr plugin downtime checks) — the jitter subsumes the stagger intent; that item is marked absorbed/blocked-by this item.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Round-robin grouping key is the **priority level** (critical/high/medium/low), not sortIndex (operator answer).
- Coordination state lives in the existing shared `.worklog/` files — no new daemons, no DB schema change.
- Jitter range is exactly ±50% of the configured poll interval (operator answer).
- Fail-closed / fail-open conventions preserved at every boundary (existing design doctrine); round-robin must never weaken the existing dispatched-marker exclusion or the CAS claim.
- No scope creep: no changes to `wl` CLI selection order (`src/commands`), the Pi TUI mirror, or the grouping/fetcher list ordering.

## Existing state

- `dispatchDowntimeWork` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) runs tiers in order: audit → implement → plan (`intake_complete`) → intake (`idea`).
- Selection (`selectNextCandidate` / `selectAuditCandidate` / `selectImplementCandidate`) sorts candidates ascending by `sortIndex` and picks the first — deterministic, so a tied group always resolves to the same item; the fastest instance wins the CAS claim every time.
- Scheduler (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`) registers a fixed-interval `downtime` task (`intervalMs = downtimePollIntervalMs`, default 30s); all instances poll in lockstep.
- Dispatch markers (`downtime-dispatches.log`) + CAS claim (WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN) prevent double-dispatch of the same item but do not address "same instance always wins" or tied-item rotation.

## Desired change

1. **Shared round-robin registry** (`<cwd>/.worklog/downtime-round-robin.json`): map priority level → last-dispatched item id (or rotation cursor). New read/write helpers alongside `downtime-log.ts` (same fail-open discipline). Selection consults the registry: among same-priority candidates, pick the item after the cursor; record the pick before dispatch (write-then-spawn ordering, mirroring the dispatched-marker discipline).
2. **Jittered probes**: the downtime scheduler task's effective interval = `downtimePollIntervalMs + uniform(-50%..+50%)` per tick (injectable RNG; deterministic tests). This absorbs the stagger intent of WL-0MSMHX6IR007F3H6.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — round-robin selection logic (`selectNextCandidate`, `selectAuditCandidate`, `selectImplementCandidate` gain a rotation-aware variant or shared helper); jitter helper.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — new `downtime-round-robin.json` read/write helpers (mirror existing dispatch-log helpers).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — downtime scheduler task uses jittered interval per tick.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — wire rotation registry path into `createDowntimeDeps`/`createDowntimeWorker` (cwd-scoped).
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts` — only if the interval-mutation approach needs a small hook (prefer mutating the task's `intervalMs` inside its run, which the scheduler already re-reads at reschedule time).
- Tests: `downtime-worker.test.ts`, `downtime-log.test.ts`, `worklist.test.ts` / `scheduler.test.ts`.

## Related work

- WL-0MSMHX6IR007F3H6 — Stagger herdr plugin downtime checks (open, medium): **absorbed by this item** (probe jitter supersedes).
- WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN — Downtime dispatcher: conditional claim + marker exclusion (completed): the CAS/claim infra this builds on; round-robin must compose with it.
- WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT — RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches same item (completed): context for the marker/CAS design points.
- WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8 — Log herdr downtime dispatches (completed): the `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` pattern reused for the round-robin file.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** round-robin rotates *items within a priority level* and is shared across instances on one machine via the local `.worklog/` file; cross-machine fairness relies on jitter + the existing CAS claim (no cross-machine shared state) — consistent with operator answers.
- **Risk:** cursor-write races between instances on the same file. Mitigation: reuse the existing flock/atomic-rename pattern used by the dispatch log; a lost update degrades to a repeated pick, never a wrong-priority pick.
- **Risk:** jitter delays dispatch by up to +50% of the poll interval when a machine would otherwise be first. Accepted per operator instruction (fairness over latency).
- **Risk (scope creep):** do not extend round-robin into `wl` CLI ordering or list rendering; tie-break is a herdr-client concern. Extra opportunities (e.g. cross-machine leases) are recorded as linked work items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Round-robin scope — across instances (competing herdr instances take turns) or across items (tied-priority items dispatched in rotation)?" — Answer (user): "(b) across items — when several items tie on priority, they get dispatched in rotation." Source: interactive reply, 2026-08-14.
- Q2: "Coordination mechanism — shared state in `.worklog/` or purely instance-local probabilistic?" — Answer (user): "existing is fine" (shared `.worklog/` files acceptable). Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Random delay bounds — range and placement (between probes only, or also pre-dispatch backoff)?" — Answer (user): "±50% of the poll interval" (between probes). Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "Tie definition — same priority level regardless of sortIndex, or identical sortIndex?" — Answer (user): "(a) same priority level (critical/high/medium/low)". Source: interactive reply.
- Q5: "Rotation state scope — shared (one rotation per priority group in `.worklog/`) or per-instance?" — Answer (user): "(a) shared — all instances on the machine rotate together". Source: interactive reply.
- Q6: "Relationship to existing stagger item WL-0MSMHX6IR007F3H6?" — Answer (user): "absorb". Source: interactive reply.

## Problem statement

During the 2026-08-20 system hang, \"Under memory pressure, flushing caches\" appeared 10+ times in the journal between 13:27 and 13:40 with no alert and no early warning. The system ran for 21 days with accumulating memory pressure and no monitoring to catch it before it became unusable.

## Goal

Install lightweight memory-pressure monitoring so a repeat of the 2026-08-20 memory exhaustion is detected and alerted on well before the system becomes unresponsive.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A monitoring mechanism is installed (e.g. cron/systemd timer script checking /proc/meminfo MemAvailable, or earlyoom/PSI-based monitoring via /proc/pressure/memory)
- [ ] An alert fires when MemAvailable drops below a threshold (e.g. 2 GB) - alert method documented (logger/journald entry, desktop notification, or both)
- [ ] Historical trend is captured so memory exhaustion can be diagnosed after the fact (e.g. collectd/sysstat already captures sar data - verify and document retention)
- [ ] The alert mechanism is tested end-to-end once (verified alert emission)
- [ ] Setup and thresholds documented in a comment on this work item or docs

## Suggested approach

```bash
# /etc/cron.d/memwatch (example)
* * * * * root [ $(awk '/MemAvailable/ {print int($2/1024)}' /proc/meminfo) -lt 2048 ] && logger -p user.warning "LOW MEMORY: $(awk '/MemAvailable/ {printf \"%.0fMB
\", $2/1024}' /proc/meminfo)"
```

Consider also monitoring /proc/pressure/memory (PSI) for sustained pressure events, which is what journald's \"Under memory pressure\" messages derive from.

## Key files

- /proc/meminfo, /proc/pressure/memory, /var/log/sysstat (sar data if installed)
- Discovered from: RCA of system hang 2026-08-20 (session analysis; no parent work item)

# Implement auto-downgrade of critical priority on terminal transitions

## Goal
When a work item with `priority=critical` transitions to a terminal state (status=completed or stage=in_review), automatically downgrade its priority to `high`.

## Implementation Details

### 1. Downgrade Logic

Add a helper function to detect and perform the auto-downgrade:
- Location: `packages/shared/src/database.ts` alongside the existing `cascadePriorityDowngrade`
- Function: `downgradeIfTerminal(item)` or inline check
- Logic: if item's new state has `status=completed` or `stage=in_review` AND `priority=critical`, set `priority=high`

### 2. Call Sites

Invoke from terminal-transition paths:
- `src/commands/update.ts` — after status/stage update, before response
- `src/commands/close.ts` — after close logic, before response

Prefer explicit call sites to avoid interfering with internal DB `update()` cascade calls.

### 3. Reporting

Report the downgrade in both output formats, mirroring the existing `downgradedChildren` pattern:
- JSON output: add `downgradedItem` field (or similar) with `{id, priority}` 
- Human-readable: add a summary line like `Downgraded priority from critical to high`

### 4. Constraints

- Only affect `critical` → `high` downgrade
- No change to other priorities (high/medium/low remain untouched)
- Only trigger on terminal transitions: `--status completed`, `--stage in_review`, or `wl close`
- Non-terminal transitions (e.g., `idea` → `plan_complete`) must NOT change priority

### Key Files
- `src/commands/update.ts` — terminal transition handling
- `src/commands/close.ts` — close path
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — helper function location
- `src/validators/priority.ts` — priority constants

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, when the local LLM is idle, I want the herdr downtime
worker to avoid starting **non-critical** implementations while the
completed/in_review review queue is already deep enough to fill the
selection list, so the producer-review bottleneck is not overloaded.
Auditing, intake, and planning can still be dispatched — only the
implement tier is gated.

## Background

- Dispatch tier order (dispatchDowntimeWork): scheduled prompts → audit →
  implement → plan → intake. The code-freeze gate (WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY)
  already skips audit+implement during a release; this is a second,
  orthogonal implement-tier-only throttle on the producer-review queue.
- The herdr selection list displays up to `browseItemCount` items
  (default 20, clamp 1–50, packages/herdr/src/settings.ts).
- Review-queue count = completed/in_review **root** items
  (`wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only --json`) —
  same query family as the audit tier (WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG) and the
  selection list's mandatory review subset (WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B).
  Operator decision (2026-08): count is ROOT-ONLY, not all items.
- Implement candidates carry `priority` (critical/high/medium/low) via
  parseImplementCandidatesOutput.

## Design notes

- Gate: when `reviewQueueCount >= browseItemCount`, the implement tier
  selects only candidates with `priority === 'critical'`; non-critical
  candidates are excluded and dispatch falls through to plan/intake.
- Critical priority BYPASSES the gate — a critical implement always stays
  eligible regardless of queue depth.
- Fail-closed: a wl error counting the review queue → gate active (only
  critical implements), consistent with the code-freeze "ambiguous ⇒
  frozen" convention.
- `browseItemCount` is re-read live from settings on each dispatch (no
  plugin restart needed), matching the existing config() re-read pattern.
- The gate skip must NOT look like an empty backlog: when implement
  candidates exist but are gated AND plan/intake are empty, the outcome
  must be a neutral reason (never 'no-candidate'), so the worker's
  no-candidate cooldown is not triggered — polling continues and a
  critical implement / new plan / intake item dispatches immediately
  (mirrors the code-freeze 'code-freeze' reason convention).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A critical-priority implement candidate is always eligible regardless
   of review-queue depth (critical bypasses the gate).
2. When reviewQueueCount < browseItemCount, implement-tier selection is
   UNCHANGED: all priorities eligible; risk/effort/dispatched-marker
   filters unchanged.
3. When reviewQueueCount >= browseItemCount, non-critical implement
   candidates are excluded; if only non-critical candidates remain,
   getNextImplementCandidate resolves null and dispatch falls through to
   plan/intake (no-candidate only when plan AND intake are genuinely
   empty; a gate skip with an empty plan/intake backlog is a neutral
   reason, never 'no-candidate').
4. The gate applies ONLY to the implement tier — audit, plan, intake,
   and scheduled-prompt dispatch are unaffected.
5. The review-queue count query is bounded by DOWNTIME_WL_TIMEOUT_MS and
   fail-closed (error ⇒ gate active).
6. Tests cover: gate boundary (count == listSize − 1 vs count == listSize),
   critical bypass, root-only counting, fall-through outcome, and the
   neutral (no-cooldown) reason on a gate skip with empty plan/intake.

## Related work

- WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6 — Implement tier end-to-end in herdr downtime worker
- WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG — Audit tier (completed/in_review without valid audit)
- WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY — Code-freeze gate
- WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B — Selection list must always show all
  completed/in_review and critical items

As an operator, I do not want the herdr downtime worker to inhibit dispatch based on the GLOBAL active_query signal when the proxy serves the local-only signal, so that remote/cloud streams never block local downtime dispatch. The backward-compatibility fallback to the global `active_query` for pre-fix proxies must be removed.

## Background

- `isIdleStatus`/`globalIdleChecks` in packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts: `const queryActive = status.local_active_query !== undefined ? status.local_active_query : status.active_query;` — the fallback to `active_query` exists for proxies that predate the `local_active_queries` counter (LP-0MSL2ZLLS009RVKR, delivered in WL-0MSL2ZQIF006QB4Q).
- The global `active_query` is true whenever ANY request is in flight — local AND remote provider streams. Remote streams keep it true while the local model is idle with free slots, so the fallback can block legitimate downtime dispatch (RCA WL-0MSK9TUCA00206M7).
- The local-only signal (`local_active_query`) is the correct busy signal for the local model.

## Design notes

- Remove the `local_active_query !== undefined ? ... : active_query` fallback; use only `local_active_query`.
- Fail-closed question to resolve: is a MISSING `local_active_query` now treated as busy (no dispatch) or idle (dispatch)? Decision: treat a missing signal as busy (fail-closed, consistent with the rest of the worker) — a pre-fix proxy must not cause dispatch on an unverifiable signal.
- parseLlamaStatus currently accepts an absent `local_active_query` (`undefined`); a work item must decide whether absence becomes null (busy) or a documented explicit non-dispatch.
- Update parseLlamaStatus doc + isIdleStatus/globalIdleChecks comments (LP-0MSL2ZLLS009RVKR reference).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `globalIdleChecks` uses ONLY `local_active_query` once present in the payload; the `active_query` fallback is removed.
2. A payload WITHOUT `local_active_query` fails closed: the worker treats the status as busy (no dispatch) and the behaviour is documented — no silent degraded dispatch on pre-fix proxies.
3. Remote/cloud streams (global active_query true, local false) are never a dispatch inhibitor.
4. Test suite covers: local_active_query present (both values), local_active_query absent (busy), and the removal of the fallback branch.
data.title: Downtime idle detection: remove fallback to global active_query when local_active_query absent (fail-closed busy)

data.description:
As an operator, I do not want a transient failure in the downtime dispatch pipeline to strand a work item in `in_progress` with no agent working it and no automatic recovery.

## Background

- dispatchClaimedTier (packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts) pipeline: CAS claim → marker write → spawn.
- Gap 1 from the dispatch decision-point evaluation: if the marker write fails (D16) AFTER the CAS claim succeeds, the outcome is reason 'marker-write-failed' and the item stays `in_progress` — but the claim is never rolled back. The item is then invisible to every later tier: plan/implement tiers select `status === 'open'`, the audit tier selects `completed`. Only manual intervention recovers it.
- Same class of issue on 'spawn-failed' (D17): the marker stands (kind `implement`/`plan`/`audit` at the dispatched-at stage), so even after a human reverts the item to `open`, the dispatched-marker exclusion keeps it out of selection until the stage changes — a transient send-to-pi.sh failure (e.g. ENOENT) permanently removes a never-worked item from the idle-slot queue.
- Existing design intent (RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT design point 2): "an unmarked item is never dispatched" — this is sound; the gap is the missing RECOVERY path, not the fail-closed abort.

## Design notes

- Option A (rollback): on 'marker-write-failed', restore the item to its pre-claim state (CAS reverse: `wl update <id> --status open --if-status in_progress [--if-stage ...]`) so the next idle period can select it again.
- Option B (requeue for spawn-failed): on 'spawn-failed', write a distinct marker variant (e.g. `outcome: 'spawn-failed'` entries are already appended) and have the marker-exclusion readers treat a spawn-failed marker as NON-excluding (item is re-eligible) while still logging the failure — the rolling log already distinguishes attempted vs opened (WL-0MSLWJ3I70031Z8U AC2).
- Both options preserve the fail-closed invariant (a marker-less item is never dispatched twice concurrently); the CAS claim already serializes re-selection.
- Decide and document whether the re-dispatch window should be immediate (next idle) or after a short backoff to avoid spawn-failure hot loops.

## Acceptance criteria

1. 'marker-write-failed' leaves the item in a state selectable by a future tier (rolled back to open+original stage, or equivalently recovered) — never stranded in_progress with no agent.
2. 'spawn-failed' does not permanently exclude the item from selection; the failure trace remains in the rolling log and the outcome is still not success.
3. No regression: an item with a STANDING success marker is still excluded (never double-dispatched); CAS claim still serializes concurrent panes.
4. Tests cover marker-write-failed and spawn-failed recovery paths end-to-end (claim → failure → re-selection on the next idle period).
data.title: Downtime dispatch: recover items stranded by marker-write-failed or spawn-failed (no permanent->in_progress stranding)

# Ensure only single audit active during downtime dispatch

## Problem statement

During downtime dispatching through the leader, only a single audit should ever be active at any one time. The dispatch logic must check for existing active audits (dispatched but not yet completed) and skip dispatching another audit if one is already in progress, ensuring audits are strictly sequential rather than allowing fan-out.

## Users

- **Operator running multiple herdr instances** — wants audit work to progress deterministically, one at a time, without competing audits consuming LLM capacity.
- **Operator relying on audit results for release decisions** — needs audit outcomes to be reliable and complete; concurrent audits increase the risk of missed findings.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Audit sequential enforcement** — Before dispatching an audit-tier item, the dispatcher checks whether any audit-tier item is currently `in_progress` (dispatched but not yet completed/reviewed). If one exists, the audit tier is skipped and the dispatcher falls through to the next tier.
2. **Leader-only check** — Only the elected leader performs the active-audit check; non-leader instances do not dispatch audits at all (unchanged behavior).
3. **Check mechanism** — The dispatcher queries the worklog for any audit-tier item (completed/in_review candidates) that has a corresponding dispatch entry in `downtime-dispatches.log` with kind `audit`. If the dispatched audit entry is older than a stale threshold (2 hours), it is treated as stale and ignored (audit pane may have crashed without updating the work item).
4. **Active audit blocks new dispatch** — If an active (non-stale) audit is found, the audit tier is skipped and dispatch falls through to the implement tier. The skip reason `audit-in-flight` is logged for observability.
5. **Existing guards preserved** — The single-flight guard (`dispatchInFlight`), CAS claim, dispatched-marker exclusion, and code-freeze gate continue to work unchanged.
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Audit tier only** — this constraint applies only to the audit dispatch tier; implement/plan/intake tiers are unaffected.
- **Existing single-flight guard** — the in-process `dispatchInFlight` guard remains in place; this adds a cross-idle-period guard (prevents re-dispatch on the next idle tick while a previous audit is still running).
- **Coordination file aware** — in the leader-election refactor context, the check must consider audits dispatched by any instance (not just the current instance), using the coordination file or dispatch log as the source of truth.
- **Fail-safe** — if the active-audit check cannot complete (e.g., worklog query fails), the dispatcher falls through to the next tier rather than blocking all dispatch.

## Existing state

- `dispatchDowntimeWork` dispatches audit-tier items via `dispatchClaimedTier(deps, 'audit', ...)`.
- The `dispatchInFlight` guard prevents concurrent dispatch calls within the same idle period.
- CAS claim moves dispatched items to `in_progress`, removing them from `wl next`/`wl list` selection.
- Dispatched markers in `downtime-dispatches.log` track dispatched items with kind and timestamp.
- The audit tier runs first, before implement/plan/intake tiers.
- Under the leader-election refactor (WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL), only the leader dispatches, but multiple idle periods could span across a running audit.

## Desired change

1. **Active audit check** — Before selecting an audit candidate, query whether any audit-tier item is currently active (dispatched and `in_progress`). This can be done by: (a) scanning the dispatched-marker log for recent audit dispatches where the item is still `in_progress`, or (b) querying the worklog for `in_progress` items that match audit-tier criteria.
2. **Audit tier skip** — If an active audit is found, skip the audit tier and proceed to the implement tier (unchanged fallback behavior).
3. **Logging** — Log the skip reason (`audit-in-flight`) for observability.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchDowntimeWork`: add active-audit check before `getNextAuditCandidate`; skip audit tier if active audit found; log skip reason.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — possibly a new dep method `getActiveAudits(cwd)` or reuse existing dispatched-marker logic.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — tests: audit skipped when one active, audit dispatched when none active, active-audit check failure falls through gracefully.

## Related work

- **WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL** — Refactor Downtime Dispatcher: leader election with shared coordination file (open, plan_complete) — the primary context; this constraint applies to the leader-only dispatch model.
- **WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG** — Allow /skill:audit on complete/in_review items without a valid audit (completed) — establishes the audit tier.
- **WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY** — Downtime dispatcher triggers multiple identical sessions (completed) — parent for dispatched-marker exclusion.

### Related work (automated report)

- **WL-0MT32F908002YFFA** — Downtime dispatch: recover items stranded by marker-write-failed or spawn-failed (open) — directly relevant to stale-audit timeout design; a crashed audit pane that fails to update the work item state is the scenario the timeout protects against.
- **WL-0MSN3FWV5008KQE9** — Herdr plugin: activity-gated proxy mode switching (completed) — proxy idle/busy semantics relevant to dispatch timing.
- **WL-0ML7QRBQR183KXPB** — Auto-unblock on dependency changes (completed) — dependency resolution patterns may inform how active-audit detection handles blocked items.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** An audit is considered "active" from the moment it is dispatched (marked in `downtime-dispatches.log`) until the item transitions from `in_progress` to a terminal state (`completed`/`in_review` with a fresh audit, or reverted to `completed/in_review` for re-audit).
- **Assumption:** The dispatch log or worklog query is fast enough to not impact dispatch latency (should be sub-second for typical worklog sizes).

- **Risk:** The active-audit check adds complexity to the dispatch loop. Mitigation: keep the check simple (one worklog query or log scan) and fail-open (skip audit tier on query failure).
- **Scope-creep guard:** Extending this constraint to implement/plan/intake tiers is out of scope. Only audit-tier sequentialization is required.
- **Risk (leader-election context):** Multiple instances could have stale active-audit entries from crashed instances. Mitigation: the check should use the coordination file or dispatch log timestamps to detect stale entries.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should the single-audit constraint apply only to audits, or to all dispatch tiers?" — Answer (user): "Audit only. Implement/plan/intake are not affected." Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "How should we detect an 'active' audit? By worklog status or dispatch log?" — Answer (user): "Check for audit-tier items that are dispatched but not yet completed — use the dispatched markers or worklog query. The check must work in the leader-election context." Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "What happens if the active-audit check fails?" — Answer (user): "Fail-open: skip the audit tier and fall through to implement. Do not block all dispatch." Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "Should there be a timeout on active audits? (e.g., if an audit pane crashes, the item stays in_progress forever)" — Answer (user): "Yes — add a stale-audit timeout. If an audit dispatch entry is older than a reasonable threshold (e.g., 2 hours), treat it as stale and allow re-dispatch." Source: interactive reply.
data.title: Ensure only single audit active during downtime dispatch

# Active-audit single-flight tests

## Summary

Test battery pinning the single-active-audit guarantee in the downtime dispatcher before implementation: audits dispatch when none is active, are skipped (falling through to the implement tier) when one is active, treat stale dispatch markers as expired, and fail open when the active-audit check itself fails.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Audit dispatched when none active** — When no audit-tier item is currently `in_progress` (no non-stale `kind=audit` dispatch entry maps to an `in_progress` item), the audit tier dispatches as today.
2. **One active audit → audit tier skipped** — When an audit-tier item is currently `in_progress` (dispatched but not yet completed/reviewed), the audit tier is skipped and the dispatcher falls through to the next tier (implement).
3. **Stale dispatch entry ignored** — An audit dispatch entry in `downtime-dispatches.log` with `kind` `audit` older than the stale threshold (2 hours) is treated as stale and ignored; a new audit dispatch proceeds.
4. **Active-audit-check failure fails open** — When the active-audit check cannot complete (e.g., worklog query fails), the audit tier is skipped and dispatch falls through to implement without blocking all dispatch.
5. **Audit-in-flight reason logged** — An audit-in-flight skip with an empty implement/plan/intake backlog reports outcome reason `audit-in-flight` (never `no-candidate`), so the no-candidate cooldown is not entered (mirrors the `code-freeze` precedent); skip logged for observability.
6. **Existing guards unchanged** — Regression tests for the single-flight guard (`dispatchInFlight`), CAS claim, dispatched-marker exclusion, and code-freeze gate pass unchanged.
7. **Full project test suite passes** — The complete test suite passes with the new tests.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `describe` blocks to `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` covering scenarios 1–5 above.
- Extend `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts` for marker-age/stale-window helper coverage.
- Fixtures: dispatched-log entries (`kind=audit`, `dispatchedAt` ages: fresh / stale / unrelated-kind); mock worklog `in_progress` queries (empty, matching, failing).
- Assert outcome reasons (`audit` dispatched vs `audit-in-flight` skip vs `no-candidate` absence) and tier fall-through.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts`

## Dependencies

None (first item; test-first ordering).

## Deliverables

Test code only — no production changes.

# Active-audit detection & audit-tier skip

## Summary

Add an active-audit detection dependency (`getActiveAudit(cwd)`) that reads `kind=audit` dispatch markers from `downtime-dispatches.log` within a 2-hour stale window and confirms the item is still `in_progress` via a single worklog query; gate the audit tier in `dispatchDowntimeWork` and log the skip reason `audit-in-flight`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Audit sequential enforcement** — Before dispatching an audit-tier item, the dispatcher checks whether any audit-tier item is currently `in_progress` (dispatched but not yet completed/reviewed). If one exists, the audit tier is skipped and the dispatcher falls through to the next tier.
2. **Check mechanism** — The dispatcher queries the worklog for audit-tier items that have a corresponding dispatch entry in `downtime-dispatches.log` with `kind` `audit`; a dispatched audit entry older than a stale threshold (2 hours) is treated as stale and ignored (audit pane may have crashed without updating the work item).
3. **Stale window constant** — A named constant `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_STALE_WINDOW_MS` (= 2 hours) defines the stale threshold; entries older than it are ignored.
4. **Active audit blocks new dispatch** — If an active (non-stale) audit is found, the audit tier is skipped and dispatch falls through to the implement tier; the skip reason `audit-in-flight` is logged for observability, and when the remaining backlog is empty the outcome is `audit-in-flight` (never `no-candidate`), so the no-candidate cooldown is not entered (mirrors `code-freeze`).
5. **Fail-open on check failure** — If the active-audit check cannot complete (e.g., worklog query fails), the audit tier is skipped and dispatch falls through to the implement tier; dispatch is never blocked.
6. **Existing guards preserved** — The single-flight guard (`dispatchInFlight`), CAS claim, dispatched-marker exclusion, and code-freeze gate continue to work unchanged.
7. **Leader-only check scope** — Only the elected leader performs the active-audit check; the check is placed in the audit-tier dispatch path only (leader-only under WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL), with no new instance-local state, so non-leader instances do not dispatch audits (unchanged behavior).
8. **Full project test suite passes** — The complete test suite passes with the new changes.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `DowntimeWorkerDeps` with `getActiveAudit(cwd)` (returns `{ ok, active }`-shaped result).
- Implement in `createDowntimeDeps` (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts`) using `readDowntimeLogEntries` + one `wl list --status in_progress --json` query intersected with non-stale audit dispatched ids; fail-open (never throws).
- Wire the gate into `dispatchDowntimeWork` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) immediately before `getNextAuditCandidate`, within the audit tier branch; add the `audit-in-flight` outcome reason + stderr/log observability.
- Add `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_STALE_WINDOW_MS` constant (2h).
- Verify against F1 test battery; run full suite.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`

## Dependencies

- F1 (Active-audit single-flight tests) — test-first prerequisite.

## Deliverables

Production code changes + passing full test suite.

# Allow bounded concurrent downtime dispatches during cheap mode (use both local slots)

## Problem statement

Proxy usage analysis of the 04:00-06:00 cheap-mode window (2026-08-22 report, `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`) shows the local Qwen3 model busy only ~25-38% of the window. Root cause is structural, not demand: the downtime worker dispatches strictly **single-flight** (one work item at a time, WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY), each dispatched session consumes exactly **one** local slot, and cheap mode provides **two** slots. The second cheap slot is essentially never used, and the per-item tail (agent tool-execution gaps between generation bursts, 10s-5min each) is pure idle that nothing else can fill.

24 herdr `audit-WL-*` sessions ran nearly sequentially: short generation bursts (3-10s) separated by long tool-execution gaps. Inter-run scheduler dead time (60s idle threshold + 10s poll + spawn) added another ~70s per dispatch cycle.

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — pays for remote fallback tokens; wants maximum value from the always-on local iGPU during cheap hours (01:00-10:00).
- **Herdr downtime users** — want more audits/work items completed per night.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. During cheap mode, the downtime worker MAY dispatch a second work item to fill an otherwise-idle second local slot, subject to a bounded concurrency cap (start with 2 concurrent dispatches).
2. Dispatch of the second item respects the same idle-gate contract (requires `requiredFreeSlots` free slots observed for the idle-threshold duration) — it must NOT queue or dispatch into a busy slot.
3. The concurrency cap is configurable via downtime settings (default 1 = current behavior, so fast/operator-interactive mode is unchanged unless explicitly enabled).
4. Fast mode (3 slots) and operator-interactive sessions keep priority: downtime never displaces an active operator session slot; only genuinely free slots are used.
5. Tests: bounded-concurrency dispatch logic (cap honored, second dispatch only fires when ≥1 slot free for N polls), no regression to existing single-flight claim safety (WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY).
6. Measured outcome: nightly cheap-window busy % for the local model increases vs. baseline (target ≥ 2x the current ~25-38%).

## Notes

- Coupling: dispatched audits run `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1`, so ONE audit uses at most 1 slot (parent then child serially). Two concurrent audits therefore use at most 2 slots = exactly cheap mode's capacity (WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS). Raising fan-out (see the AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM item) changes this budget and must be coordinated — total in-flight local streams must not exceed the cheap pool.

# Dispatched audits: use both cheap slots during Phase 2 deep analysis

## Problem statement

The downtime worker pins `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1` for dispatched audits (WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS) so an audit's Phase 2 child deep-analysis runs strictly sequentially (parent first, then one child at a time). This guarantees one audit fits cheap mode's 2-slots (parent + 1 child = 2) — but it also means a single dispatched audit NEVER uses more than one slot at a time during almost its entire run: Phase 1 is a single stream, and Phase 2 children serialize.

Proxy usage analysis of the 04:00-06:00 cheap window (2026-08-22) shows the local model busy only ~25-38% while these audits ran — the second slot sat idle. The audit chain ran 17 child sessions with ~12s gaps, then multi-minute gaps between dispatched runs.

Raising the fan-out to 2 would let one child run concurrently with the parent (2 slots busy) during deep analysis — but the current bound (WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS) exists precisely to keep child-heavy audits inside the cheap 2-slot pool. Parent + 2 children = 3 concurrent streams would fall back to remote. This item must therefore be coordinated with the concurrent-dispatch item so the combined in-flight stream budget never exceeds cheap capacity (2 slots).

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — wants higher overnight local utilization without pushing more traffic to fallback (429-capped) remotes.
- **Herdr downtime users** — want child-heavy audits to complete faster.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Phase 2 deep-analysis concurrency for dispatched audits is mode-aware: 1 (current serial behavior) in fast mode or whenever the combined dispatch budget would exceed the cheap 2-slot pool; 2 when a second slot is genuinely free (coordinated with the concurrent-dispatch item).
2. Parent + N children as a single audit run never produces more concurrent local streams than the cheap-mode slot budget (2 in cheap mode).
3. No audit-skill changes (agent-infrastructure boundary — the skill already honours the env var); change lives in `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`).
4. Tests: env var value is mode/budget-dependent; spawn options for cheap mode with a free second slot include `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM: '2'`; fast mode or full pool keeps `'1'`.
5. Measured outcome: dispatched audit Phase 2 wall-clock drops (children overlap the parent) and/or cheap-window busy % rises vs. the 25-38% baseline, without increasing remote fallback rate.

## Notes

- History: WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS (completed) set `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1` with rationale "cheap mode = 2 slots = parent + 1 child" — the audit skill default is 2, which the bound overrode to prevent 3-stream fallback. This item revisits that bound for the slot-idle case rather than reverting it.
- Default `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` handling lives in `audit_runner.py` (`AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM_ENV` / legacy alias) — pinned env in the pane spawn wins over the skill default.
- Related: WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG (same-slot idle tracking), WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS (fan-out bound), plus the proxy usage report's recommendation #3.

# Faster downtime dispatch cadence: reduce poll interval and idle threshold

## Problem statement

The downtime worker polls the proxy status every `DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` (default 10s, hard floor `DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_FLOOR_MS` = 10s) and requires the model to be continuously idle for `DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` (default 60s, floor 1s) before dispatching. Per dispatch cycle this imposes ~70s of scheduler dead time (60s idle threshold + 10s poll + spawn/claim overhead).

During the 04:00-06:00 cheap window (2026-08-22 proxy usage analysis) inter-run gaps of 141s, 146s and 312s were observed between consecutive dispatched runs — a large fraction (est. ~13% of the window) attributable to this threshold+poll+spawn cadence, on top of the model being idle ~50-68% of the time. The current 10s poll floor is a hard-coded guard ("must not hammer the proxy") rather than a measured load limit; the 60s idle threshold is a conservative default from the early worker design.

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — wants more work dispatched into the idle overnight windows; lower latency between dispatch opportunities.
- **Herdr downtime users** — more items completed per night.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Both knobs stay configurable via downtime settings (existing `pollIntervalMs` / `idleThresholdMs` pattern) with **lowered floors**:
   - poll interval floor reduced from 10s to a measured-safe value (target 5s; assert proxy `/llama/local/status` call volume stays negligible — status endpoint is cheap and local);
   - idle threshold floor reduced to ≥1s (current floor) but adjusted production default lowered from 60s to a tuned value (target 15-30s) for the cheap window.
2. Defaults: cheap/downtime mode adopts the faster cadence; interactive or operator-session-sensitive paths unchanged.
3. The idle-gate semantics are preserved: dispatch still only occurs after the model has been continuously idle for the (shorter) threshold — no dispatch into a busy slot, no claim race with the existing single-flight safety (WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY).
4. Tests updated: floor enforcement (values below floor rejected/clamped), cadence honored in the poll loop, idle-gate still requires the threshold to elapse, no dispatch while slots busy.
5. Measured outcome: mean inter-dispatch gap in the cheap window drops vs. baseline (146s/312s observed), and/or more sessions dispatched per night, without breaching proxy status-endpoint load limits.

## Notes

- Constants in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`: `DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_FLOOR_MS = 10_000`, `DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_FLOOR_MS = 1_000`, `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 10_000`, `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS = 60_000`.
- The 10s floor comment says "must not hammer the proxy" — quantify actual load before lowering; the status endpoint (`/llama/local/status`) is a cheap local JSON read, so the floor is expected to be safely reducible.
- Recommended: couple with the concurrent-dispatch item (bounded concurrency) so the faster cadence feeds more than one slot rather than just firing more single dispatches.
- Related: WL-0MSG80254005ZNE9 (proxy status poller), WL-0MSG80J5W007DVJ4 (timer loop), WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG (idle tracker); evidence in `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`.

data.description:
## Goal

Document the SQLite WAL checkpoint behavior in Worklog and explain the root cause of the 16MB WAL observed during the 206-process spawn storm.

## Investigation

### Current Configuration (src/persistent-store.ts, ~line 130)

The database opens with:
- `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` — enables Write-Ahead Logging for concurrency
- `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` — enforces referential integrity
- `PRAGMA busy_timeout` — 5000ms (non-TUI) or 250ms (TUI), configurable via `WL_SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS`

**No explicit checkpoint logic exists.** No `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint` or `PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint` is set anywhere in the codebase.

### What SQLite Does by Default

- WAL auto-checkpoint triggers after **1000 pages** of writes (SQLite default)
- At default page size (4096 bytes), this is ~**4MB** of accumulated writes
- Auto-checkpoint runs when a connection checks between transactions
- On close, SQLite performs a checkpoint that merges the WAL back into the main database

### Root Cause of 16MB WAL Under 206 Concurrent Writers

1. Each of the 206 concurrent `wl` processes opens a SQLite connection
2. All writes go into the shared WAL file (`worklog.db-wal`)
3. Each connection checks for auto-checkpoint between transactions
4. But writes accumulate faster than any single connection can checkpoint
5. With 206 writers, WAL segments from concurrent writers stack up, exceeding the 1000-page threshold many times
6. The WAL reaches ~16MB because concurrent writers push writes faster than auto-checkpoint can reclaim pages
7. When all processes exit, checkpoint-on-close merges everything back (WAL files disappear)

### Why This Matters

- **Read cost**: SQLite reads must scan the WAL, so a large WAL slows every read query
- **Cache invalidation**: mtime/size of `worklog.db` alone is unreliable while a large WAL holds live writes (read-cache.ts already handles this correctly)
- **Crash/recovery**: a large WAL means longer recovery time on abnormal exit

### Code References

- `src/persistent-store.ts` — WAL mode + busy_timeout configuration (lines ~125-135)
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — same configuration
- `src/read-cache.ts` — WAL-aware cache invalidation (already correct)
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — write patterns (importData transactions, individual saves)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. This work item describes the exact SQLite WAL configuration (pragmas set, defaults used).
2. Root cause of the 16MB WAL is identified and explained (concurrent writers outpace auto-checkpoint).
3. All ACs from the parent (WL-0MSG8EG7P002MX2I) related to checkpoint understanding are covered.
data.title: Document WAL checkpoint behavior and root cause of 16MB WAL

## Goal

Measure the impact of a large WAL on read latency and produce before/after numbers for the parent AC.

## Approach

1. Create a temporary SQLite database with WAL mode enabled (mimicking Worklog schema)
2. Write N work items (e.g., 500-1000) to build up a large WAL (target > 4MB)
3. Run read queries (getAllWorkItems, search, getWorkItem by ID) and measure latency
4. Force a checkpoint (PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE))
5. Run the same read queries again and measure latency
6. Compare before/after numbers

## Expected Findings

Based on SQLite behavior, a large WAL adds overhead because:
- Each read must scan the WAL to find the latest version of each page
- The WAL is read sequentially, which is fast on SSD but slower than reading the main DB from page cache
- Expected impact: 10-50% slower reads with a 16MB WAL vs a checkpointed database

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Benchmark script or code exists that reproduces a large WAL scenario.
2. Read latency measured with small WAL vs large WAL is documented with numbers.
3. Results are recorded as a comment on this work item and referenced by the parent AC #2.
4. Benchmark is reproducible and documented (command to run, parameters, results).

data.description:
## Goal

Produce a concrete recommendation on WAL checkpointing strategy with rationale and risk notes.

## Options to Evaluate

### Option A: Leave as-is (rely on auto-checkpoint)
**Pros**: Minimal code change, no risk of introducing bugs.
**Cons**: WAL can grow under concurrent writer load; read latency impact unknown without benchmarking.
**Risk**: Low. WAL mode is inherently safe; the worst case is degraded read performance.

### Option B: Add explicit checkpoint after write-heavy operations
**Pros**: Controls WAL growth proactively; keeps reads fast.
**Cons**: Adds I/O overhead after operations like `wl sync` or bulk mutations.
**Risk**: Low. `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)` is safe — it won't block readers.
**Implementation**: Add `this.db.pragma('wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)')` after `importData()` transactions or after `wl sync` completes.

### Option C: Tune auto-checkpoint threshold
**Pros**: No code changes to write paths; adjusts the SQLite default.
**Cons**: Less precise control; still relies on per-connection checkpoint checks.
**Risk**: Very low. `PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=N` changes the threshold.
**Implementation**: Set a higher threshold (e.g., 10000 pages ≈ 40MB) in persistent-store.ts constructor.

### Option D: Hybrid — tune threshold + checkpoint after sync
**Pros**: Best of both worlds; threshold prevents runaway growth, explicit checkpoint after sync keeps WAL small.
**Cons**: Slightly more code changes.
**Risk**: Low.

## Recommendation

**Recommend Option C (tune auto-checkpoint) as the primary fix** with the following rationale:

1. The root cause is that the default 1000-page threshold is too conservative for concurrent writer workloads.
2. Raising it to ~10000 pages (40MB) would prevent the 16MB WAL from triggering frequent checkpoints while still capping growth.
3. WAL files up to 40MB are not a correctness risk — they only impact read latency.
4. For `wl sync` specifically (the main write-heavy operation), adding an explicit `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)` after the sync completes would ensure a clean state for the next operation.
5. This approach requires minimal code changes and has negligible risk.

## Implementation Sketch

```typescript
// In persistent-store.ts constructor, after journal_mode = WAL:
this.db.pragma('wal_autocheckpoint = 10000');  // 40MB threshold
```

And optionally after bulk write operations:
```typescript
// In importData() or after sync merge:
this.db.pragma('wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)');
```

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A recommendation is recorded on this work item: leave as-is, add explicit checkpointing, tune threshold, or hybrid — with rationale and risk notes.
2. If a code change is recommended, the implementation scope is clearly defined.
3. All ACs from the parent (WL-0MSG8EG7P002MX2I) are satisfied.
4. Any code change is tested and does not regress the full test suite (covered by parent AC #4).

## Problem

When the proxy returns a 503 'All providers exhausted' response (from proxy/provider.py _build_exhausted_response), the Worklog recovery extension's classifyError() function does not match this error against any of its 8 categories (RATE_LIMIT, SERVER_ERROR, AUTH_ERROR, CONTEXT_LENGTH, QUOTA_EXHAUSTED, TIMEOUT, TERMINATED, PARSE_ERROR). The result is ErrorCategory.UNKNOWN, which triggers:

  Unrecognized error: All providers exhausted

...and **halts the session with no retry**. The agent stalls waiting for user intervention.

## Solution

Add 'All providers exhausted' to the SERVER_ERROR category patterns so the existing retry loop (triggerInvisibleContinue with exponential backoff) picks it up. The error message contains no HTTP status digits or standard error keywords that the current patterns match against.

### File to modify

ContextHub/packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts

Add to DEFAULT_SERVER_ERROR_PATTERNS:

  /all providers exhausted/i,
  /no provider available/i,

### Optional enhancement (future)

If the proxy emits a Retry-After HTTP header or the Worklog extension gains access to it (from the JSON body), the retry loop could use that value as the initial backoff delay instead of the default 2-second baseDelayMs.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Error message 'All providers exhausted' is classified as ErrorCategory.SERVER_ERROR (not UNKNOWN).
2. The Worklog recovery module triggers triggerInvisibleContinue() for this error (same path as existing SERVER_ERROR).
3. The retry loop performs exponential backoff and auto-continues when providers become available.
4. No regression: existing patterns still match their expected categories.
5. Tests for error-patterns.ts pass.

## Problem statement

The herdr downtime worker audit tier selects a candidate via `selectAuditCandidate` (freshness checked at selection time), then `dispatchClaimedTier` runs CAS claim → `recordDispatch` (writes the "Auto-dispatched…" work-item comment + rolling marker) → spawn. If **during the interim** — between selection and the comment/spawn — a valid audit was recorded (e.g. a human or another process ran `wl audit-set`), the worker still writes the dispatch comment and spawns a redundant audit pane. The stale/unaudited state it selected no longer exists, so the dispatch is wasted work and the comment is misleading.

Observed (WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B): dispatch comment + marker written at 2026-08-24T20:51:49Z while a valid audit existed/landed; a later comment then made the audit appear stale and the item was re-dispatched repeatedly (audit re-recorded 2026-08-25T09:56Z).

RCA: `claimItem` CAS-guards status/stage only (TIER_EXPECTED audit = completed/in_review) — a manual `wl audit-set` does NOT change status/stage, so the claim still succeeds. There is no freshness re-check between selection and `recordDispatch`/spawn. Discovered-from: WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B.

## Desired change

In the audit-tier dispatch path, after selecting a candidate and before writing the dispatch comment/marker and spawning, re-check that the item still lacks a fresh audit (`isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` from @worklog/shared/icons). If a fresh audit now exists:
- skip the dispatch entirely (no comment, no marker, no spawn) and fall through to the next tier — treat as "already audited", not "no-candidate"/cooldown and not a strike;
- on a failed spawn (`recordDispatchFailure` / spawn-failed path), do not record/comment a failure trace if a valid audit was recorded during the interim — the pane is moot, not a failure to log as such.

Mirror the same interim freshness re-check in any other dispatcher that comments on audit dispatch (heartbeat does not comment; it invokes the runner directly — verify).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Integration test: select a stale/un-audited candidate, then record a valid audit in the "interim", then verify dispatch downgrades to a no-op (no item comment, no rolling-log `kind=audit` marker, no spawn) and falls through to the next tier without triggering the no-candidate cooldown
- [ ] Integration test: spawn-failure trace (`outcome: spawn-failed`) is NOT appended (and no failure comment) when a valid audit was recorded during the interim
- [ ] A genuinely unaudited item still dispatches exactly as today (comment + marker + spawn)
- [ ] Convention/naming: the interim check is a single dep on the worker boundary (e.g. a `hasFreshAudit(itemId)` dep) so it is testable without wl
- [ ] Full project test suite passes

## Key files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchClaimedTier` / audit-tier dispatch in `dispatchDowntimeWork` (~lines 1854–1904), `selectAuditCandidate` (~3020), worker deps (~879)
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — wire the interim freshness dep into `createDowntimeDeps` (alongside `getNextAuditCandidate`)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — interim-freshness integration tests

## Related work

- WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG — audit tier dispatch
- WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY — dispatched-marker exclusion
- WL-0MT3PHW4I002SNOV — active-audit single-flight
- WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B — observed stale-audit loop (discovered-from)

data.description:
## Problem statement

Two coupled defects leave valid audits visible as stale ("out of date audit"):

1. **Comment bumps invalidate audits.** `wl comment add` → `createComment` → `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt` (packages/shared/src/database.ts:3282, persistent-store `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt` ~3416) advances the work item `updatedAt` for ANY comment. `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` (packages/shared/src/icons.ts:269) compares `auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`; a comment added after the audit (e.g. "Audit re-evaluation (forced --force)" on WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B at 21:26:17Z vs audit 21:21:03Z) therefore flips the audit to stale ⏳ even though no content changed. The documented guarantee in icons.ts ("Flag-only flips of needsProducerReview do not move updatedAt, so a previously valid audit remains fresh") does NOT cover comments — comments are the common case that breaks it.

2. **Audit persistence does not atomically update auditedAt.** `wl audit-set` (src/commands/audit-result.ts) writes the `audit_results` row (auditedAt = now) but does not touch the work item; `wl update --audit-text` (src/commands/update.ts) also only writes `saveAuditResult`. There is no single atomic operation that both records the audit AND refreshes the freshness clock, so a comment between audit and display (or a re-evaluation that comments instead of persisting — see WL-0MT8KT2LO0056KLF) leaves the record behind `updatedAt`.

Investigation outcome — audit-content comments can be removed (no consumer parses them):
- implement skill: reads the audit **record** (`/skill:audit` → runner → `wl audit-show`; `audit_report_<id>.md`); comments are only generic context in Step 4 ("pay attention to comments"), never parsed as verdicts
- ship skill `check-audit-gate.js`: `wl audit-show` → `readyToClose`/`rawOutput`/`summary`; `wl comment add` is used only to WRITE merge logs
- heartbeat, report skill, herdr TUI (`worklist.ts`, icons): all read `auditResult`/`auditedAt` from the record

So the audit verdict must live in the audit record only; audits duplicated in comments are dead weight and actively harmful (they bump updatedAt).

Discovered-from: WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B.

## Desired change

1. **Freshness clock:** make audit freshness reflect content-only changes. Options to evaluate (pick one, document trade-offs):
   a. exclude comments (and `needsProducerReview` flag flips, already excluded) from `updatedAt` bumps via `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt`; or
   b. `isAuditFresh` uses a content/activity fingerprint rather than `updatedAt`; or
   c. `wl audit-set`/`--audit-text` perform an atomic "record audit + set updatedAt = auditedAt" so a later comment still breaks it (not fully fixing) — likely insufficient alone.
2. **Atomic audit persistence:** `wl audit-set` (and/or `wl update --audit-text`) should be a single operation that records the `audit_results` row and refreshes the item's freshness marker so "audit recorded" always implies "audit fresh" immediately.
3. **Remove audit-content comments:** stop adding the audit report/verdict to work-item comments (the verdict lives in the audit record). Keep comments for dispatches/trails (herdr "Auto-dispatched…" is a dispatch marker, not audit content — out of scope) and for human annotations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After a post-audit comment is added, the audit remains fresh: `wl show <id> --json` + a comment → `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` stays true; TUI keeps the passed icon, not ⏳ (add a regression test in packages/shared tests for the chosen mechanism)
- [ ] `wl audit-set` is atomic: after it, `auditedAt >= updatedAt` immediately (no intermediate window where a read shows stale) — or the alternative chosen mechanism guarantees the same
- [ ] The audit report/verdict is no longer duplicated into work-item comments by audit flows; existing duplicated comments on WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B are documented as legacy (no migration required unless trivially safe)
- [ ] Unit tests cover: comment-after-audit keeps fresh; audit-then-comment ordering matches the chosen freshness clock; `wl update --audit-text` path behaves identically to `wl audit-set`
- [ ] Docs updated: icons.ts guarantee comment, docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md (or equivalent), audit SKILL.md where it describes the audit record as canonical
- [ ] Full project test suite passes

## Key files (predicted)

- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `isAuditFresh`, `stageDisplayIcon` (the ⏳ stale-passed path)
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `createComment`/`touchWorkItemUpdatedAt` (~3246, 3416)
- `src/commands/audit-result.ts` — `wl audit-set` (atomic auditedAt write)
- `src/commands/update.ts` — `--audit-text` persistence path
- `src/commands/comment.ts` / `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — comment updatedAt semantics
- `packages/shared/src/icons.test.ts` (or equivalent) — freshness regression tests

## Related work

- WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B — observed stale audit (discovered-from)
- WL-0MT8KSTOE00871E7 — herdr interim freshness re-check (sibling)
- WL-0MT8KT2LO0056KLF — forced re-evaluation must persist (sibling; comment-only re-eval is the trigger that exposed this)
- WL-0MSN6ZCTN0027U2R — flag-only flips do not move updatedAt (docs this gap for the needsProducerReview case)
