# wl sync reports success while the remote is missing records

## Problem statement

`wl sync` reports "✓ Sync completed successfully" (with "No changes to sync — skipping export and push" / "Work items unchanged: 124") while the **remote git ref (`refs/worklog/data`) is missing ~102 of the local 124 work items**, including every `in_review` item. A fresh checkout on another machine (`wl init` + `wl sync`) therefore only receives the ~22 records present on the remote tip, silently losing work items.

## Users

- **Operators / agents working across multiple machines** — believe their worklog is safely synced to git and mirrored elsewhere, when it is not. Items created on one machine never reach the remote or other clones.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Machine A has a worklog with 124 work items (incl. 44 `in_review`) and a remote ref whose tip contains only 22 workitems (e.g. after a foreign-author full snapshot `27974ce` with 22 records overwrote a 769-record state `768e140`).
2. Run `wl sync` on machine A.
   - Observed: local state 124 items; remote state 22 items; `Work items added: 0`, `Work items unchanged: 124`, then `No changes to sync — skipping export and push` and `✓ Sync completed successfully`. Exit code 0.
3. Run `wl sync` on a fresh checkout (machine B): only ~22 items appear; all `in_review` items are missing.

## Root cause analysis

The delta-sync export (`exportForSync`, `countDirtyRecords`) decides what to export purely from **per-type watermarks** stored in `last_export_timestamps`:

- `workitems` watermark: `2026-08-30T23:17:08.349Z`
- max local `updatedAt`: `2026-08-30T23:14:22.345Z` → **0 records newer than the watermark → `countDirtyRecords().total === 0`** → the §5.4 zero-change fast path skips export+push entirely.

The watermark was advanced by a successful push (of a *delta* containing only the 22 merged remote records), so afterwards **every remaining local record is older than the watermark and is treated as "already synced" — even though the remote never received it**. There is **no reconciliation**: sync never verifies that records older than the watermark actually exist on the remote tip. Once the remote diverges (foreign-author commit, force-push, full snapshot from a different store with fewer records, or a delta/legacy snapshot mismatch), the local-only records become **permanently unpushable** while sync reports success.

Contributing issue: `wl sync --allow-foreign-author` merged the 22 remote records and pushed a *delta of only those 22 records*, not a full snapshot of all 124 — so the 102 missing items were still not exported, yet sync again reported success.

## Expected behaviour

- Sync detects divergence between local and remote beyond the watermark heuristic (e.g. when the local store has records absent from the remote tip), and either exports them (full re-snapshot / reconcile) or fails loudly.
- Sync never reports "✓ Sync completed successfully" / "No changes to sync" when the remote tip is missing records the local store holds.
- A fresh `wl init` + `wl sync` on another machine must reproduce the full worklog state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Divergence detection:** `wl sync` fails (or warns with non-zero exit) when the local store contains work items/comments absent from the remote tip, instead of reporting success.
- [ ] **AC2 — Self-healing export:** When divergence is detected, sync exports the missing records (full snapshot or targeted reconcile) so the remote tip converges to the local state.
- [ ] **AC3 — No false success:** `wl sync` exit code and message reflect whether the remote tip actually converged; "No changes to sync" is only emitted when local and remote are provably identical.
- [ ] **AC4 — Regression test:** A test reproduces: local store with records older than the watermark + remote tip missing those records → sync must not report success and must push the records.

## Evidence (AI_Hell repo, 2026-08-30)

- `wl sync --no-push`: `Local state: 124 work items, 583 comments` / `Remote state: 22 work items, 0 comments` / `Work items unchanged: 124` / `No changes to sync — skipping export (--no-push)` / `✓ Sync completed successfully`.
- `git show refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data:.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` at tip `1918bdd` → 22 `workitem` records (`kind: delta`).
- Local SQLite: 124 workitems; `last_export_timestamps.workitems = 2026-08-30T23:17:08.349Z`; `MAX(updatedAt) = 2026-08-30T23:14:22.345Z`; records newer than watermark: 0.
- Remote ref history shows the divergence origin: `768e140` full (769 records, 16:30) → … → `27974ce` full (22 records, 23:28) → deltas (22 records each). The 22-record full snapshot supersedes the 769-record one, so fresh clones replay from `27974ce` and get only 22 items.

## Related work

- WL-0MSOYWWS4009HTCB — author-identity gate (`--allow-foreign-author`), the flag that unblocks the merge but does not repair the remote.
- WL-0MT2KY0RQ008F50Q / WL-0MSAKUBKW006FN8Q — delta-sync design / §5.4 zero-change fast path; the watermark logic at fault.
- WL-0MT2KZ5GJ000OJIP — remote delta-chain replay (full-snapshot fallback for fresh clones); replay anchor (`27974ce`) is a smaller full snapshot, which is why fresh clones miss records.

# Author-identity gate refusal must surface at default verbosity and exit non-zero (no silent success)

## Problem statement

When the author-identity gate (WL-0MSOYWWS4009HTCB) refuses to merge foreign-authored worklog commits, `wl sync` at **default verbosity can still report success** ("✓ Sync completed successfully", exit code 0). The refusal is only visible with `--verbose` / `--dry-run`. This is a second facet of the false-success bug in WL-0MTGGGP2000642JS, on a different code path.

## Users

- **Operators running `wl sync` across machines with different git identities** — believe the merge/push succeeded when it was actually refused, so work items silently never reach the remote.

## Steps to reproduce (AI_Hell repo, 2026-08-30)

1. Remote tracking ref contains commits authored by an identity different from the store's configured `user.email` (observed: `250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com` vs `sorra@thewizardscode.com`).
2. Run `wl sync` (default verbosity).
   - Observed: `✓ Sync completed successfully`, exit 0 — no mention of the gate.
3. Run `wl sync --verbose` or `wl sync --dry-run --json`.
   - Observed: `✗ Sync failed: Refusing to merge worklog data from refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data: 2 incoming commit(s) fail the author-identity gate.` (`d48a703`, `1db5d45`).

## Expected behaviour

- A gate refusal is a **failure**: `wl sync` exits non-zero and prints the refusal reason at default verbosity (no `--verbose` required).
- The message names the offending commits and the expected vs actual author identities, and suggests `--allow-foreign-author` or a config fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Non-zero exit:** `wl sync` exits non-zero when the author-identity gate refuses the merge.
- [ ] **AC2 — Default-verbosity message:** The refusal (offending commits + expected/actual identities) is printed without `--verbose`/`--dry-run`.
- [ ] **AC3 — No false success:** The word "success" / exit 0 is never emitted for a gate-refused sync.
- [ ] **AC4 — Suggestion:** Output suggests `--allow-foreign-author` or the `syncAllowForeignAuthor` config option.
- [ ] **AC5 — Regression test:** Test where remote commits are foreign-authored → assert non-zero exit + refusal text at default verbosity.

## Related work

- WL-0MTGGGP2000642JS — parent bug: "wl sync reports success while remote is missing records — zero-change fast path skips export" (this is the gate-path facet).
- WL-0MSOYWWS4009HTCB — the author-identity gate itself (`--allow-foreign-author` flag).

# Recovery path for already-diverged worklog repos (doctor command or documented procedure)

## Problem statement

WL-0MTGGGP2000642JS addresses *future* syncs (detection + self-healing + no false success), but repositories that have **already diverged** cannot currently be repaired through a supported path. Observed 2026-08-30:

- **AI_Hell** (`/home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell`): remote `refs/worklog/data` tip holds 22 workitems while the local SQLite store has 124 (incl. 44 `in_review`). The zero-change fast path refuses to export (all local records are older than the watermark), so the missing items are permanently unpushable via `wl sync`.
- **ContextHub** (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`): remote held 1 workitem vs 2968 locally before a manual `wl sync --allow-foreign-author` recovered it (pushed 13,590 new JSONL records).

There is no documented escape hatch for "local store has records the remote never received" — the operator must improvise (forcing a full snapshot, `--allow-foreign-author`, manual ref rewrites). This item delivers a supported recovery path.

## Users

- **Operators / agents** whose worklog remote diverged from the local store (foreign-author overwrite, force-push, smaller full snapshot superseding a larger one, or delta/legacy snapshot mismatch) — need a safe, supported way to converge the remote to the local state without data loss.

## Proposed solution

Extend `wl doctor` (or add a dedicated `wl sync --force-full` / `--repair` mode) that:

1. Detects the divergence: local records absent from the remote tip (compare record IDs, not just watermarks).
2. Emits a **full snapshot** of the local store (newest full snapshot on the chain — fixes the replay anchor for fresh clones too, per AC5 of WL-0MTGGGP2000642JS).
3. Pushes with an explicit confirmation/guard so it cannot accidentally overwrite a *larger* remote (safety check: refuse if remote has records the local lacks, unless `--force`).
4. Also resets/clears invalid watermarks if they are the block.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Command/mode exists:** A supported command or mode (e.g. `wl doctor resync --full --allow-lossless` or `wl sync --force-full`) that publishes a full snapshot of the local store to the remote ref.
- [ ] **AC2 — Divergence report:** Before pushing, it reports the counts: local records, remote-tip records, records local-only, records remote-only.
- [ ] **AC3 — Lossless guard:** If the remote contains records absent locally, it refuses (or requires an explicit `--force` / `--allow-foreign-author` escalation). No silent data loss.
- [ ] **AC4 — Watermark repair:** If outdated watermarks block export, it resets them so the full snapshot is actually published.
- [ ] **AC5 — Fresh-clone verification:** After the repair, a fresh `wl init` + `wl sync` on another machine reconstructs the full local record set (this also satisfies AC5 of WL-0MTGGGP2000642JS).
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation:** The recovery procedure (and when to use it) is documented in the sync/doctor docs.
- [ ] **AC7 — Regression test:** Test: local store with records older than watermark + remote tip missing them → repair command converges the remote, and a subsequent `wl sync` reports no divergence.

## Evidence (AI_Hell repo, 2026-08-30)

- Local: 124 workitems; `last_export_timestamps.workitems = 2026-08-30T23:17:08.349Z`; `MAX(updatedAt) = 2026-08-30T23:14:22.345Z`; 0 records newer than watermark → `wl sync` fast-path skips export entirely.
- Remote tip `1918bdd` (delta): 22 `workitem` records.
- Fresh clone replays from newest full snapshot `27974ce` (22 records) → only 22 items, all `in_review` items missing.

## Related work

- WL-0MTGGGP2000642JS — parent bug: false-success sync + missing remote records; this item is the *recovery* half of that problem.
- WL-0MTGGGP2000642JS AC4/AC5 — regression coverage that this command must satisfy.
- WL-0MSOYWWS4009HTCB — author-identity gate; foreign-authored remote histories are a common cause of divergence.
- WL-0MT2KZ5GJ000OJIP — remote delta-chain replay; the full-snapshot anchor logic a repair must respect.

# Intake Brief: Remove OpenBrain (WL-0MTH28WDS008WMXA)

## Problem statement

OpenBrain is an optional integration (`src/openbrain.ts`) that spawns the `ob` CLI to submit a summary whenever a work item is marked completed. This project enabled it for local testing (`openBrainEnabled: true` in `.worklog/config.yaml`, commit `66fb51a8`) but the `ob` binary is not installed, so every `wl update`/`wl close` that completes an item emits `[openbrain] ...` errors to stderr. The integration is unused and, per producer confirmation, is to be **removed entirely** — both from the shared codebase and from this project's config.

## Users

- **Developers** running `wl update`/`wl close` in this project — they see stray `[openbrain]` errors and want clean output.
- **Worklog maintainers** — they want dead integration code (which requires an `ob` binary nobody has and whose `wl openbrain` commands were never implemented) removed from the shared CLI.

User stories:
- As a developer in this project, I want `wl update` to complete a work item without emitting `[openbrain]` errors, so my terminal output is clean.
- As a Worklog maintainer, I want the OpenBrain integration absent from the shared codebase, so there is no dead code and no misleading docs/plugin references.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Feature removed from the shared codebase**: `src/openbrain.ts` deleted; `submitToOpenBrain` imports and call sites removed from `src/commands/update.ts` and `src/commands/close.ts`; `openBrainEnabled` removed from `WorklogConfig` in `packages/shared/src/types.ts`.
2. **Project-scoped disablement**: `openBrainEnabled: true` removed from `.worklog/config.yaml` in this repository.
3. **No dangling references or dead artifacts**: `tests/unit/openbrain.test.ts`, `tests/cli/openbrain-close.test.ts`, and `docs/openbrain.md` deleted; OpenBrain references removed from `CLI.md` and `README.md`. A repo-wide search (`rg -i "openbrain|submitToOpenBrain|openBrainEnabled"`) returns no matches in tracked source/docs (excluding git history and regenerated `dist/` artifacts).
4. **Error gone**: completing a work item via `wl update` and `wl close` in this project produces no `[openbrain]` stderr output (validated by the CLI test run, AC5).
5. **Green build & docs**: full project test suite passes with the new changes; all related documentation reflects the removal (README, CLI.md, code comments, docs table).

## Constraints

- No behavior changes beyond removing the OpenBrain path — `wl close`/`wl update` semantics (recursive close, re-sort, audit handling) are untouched.
- Worktrees under `.worklog/worktrees/*` are separate feature branches — do not edit them in this change; only the main checkout is in scope.
- Config user file `.worklog/config.yaml` is the only place `openBrainEnabled` is set in this repo; `config.defaults.yaml` does not set it (verify at implementation time).
- The optional retry-queue file `.worklog/openbrain-queue.jsonl` may exist from failed submissions; it is transient data, not code — no action required beyond optionally removing it.

## Existing state

- `src/openbrain.ts` implements `submitToOpenBrain()` (spawns `ob add --stdin --title …`), `buildOpenBrainSummary()`, `appendToQueue()` (retry queue), and `resolveObBinary()` (`WL_OB_BIN` or `ob`).
- `src/commands/update.ts`: calls `submitToOpenBrain(item)` when `updates.status === 'completed'` and `config.openBrainEnabled`.
- `src/commands/close.ts`: calls `submitToOpenBrain(updated)` from the force, audit-gated recursive, and standard close paths when `config.openBrainEnabled`; the recovery path comments reference OpenBrain.
- `packages/shared/src/types.ts`: `WorklogConfig` declares `openBrainEnabled?: boolean`.
- `.worklog/config.yaml`: `openBrainEnabled: true`.
- Docs: `docs/openbrain.md`; `CLI.md` lists `wl openbrain status/resubmit` (commands were never implemented); `README.md` docs table links `docs/openbrain.md`.
- Tests: `tests/unit/openbrain.test.ts`, `tests/cli/openbrain-close.test.ts`.
- `ob` is not on PATH and `WL_OB_BIN` is unset; the globally installed `wl` (`/usr/local/bin/wl`) symlinks to this repo's built `dist/cli.js`, so a rebuild is required to actually stop the errors.

## Desired change

Remove the OpenBrain integration and its project config toggle:

- Delete `src/openbrain.ts`, `docs/openbrain.md`, `tests/unit/openbrain.test.ts`, `tests/cli/openbrain-close.test.ts`.
- In `src/commands/update.ts` / `src/commands/close.ts`: drop the `submitToOpenBrain` import and every `openBrainEnabled` fire-and-forget block (including the recovery-path comment).
- In `packages/shared/src/types.ts`: remove `openBrainEnabled?: boolean`.
- In `.worklog/config.yaml`: remove `openBrainEnabled: true`.
- In `CLI.md` / `README.md`: remove OpenBrain references.
- Rebuild (`npm run build:shared && npm run build`) so the installed `wl` no longer ships `openbrain.js` in `dist/`.

## Key Files:

- `src/openbrain.ts` — delete (entire module)
- `src/commands/update.ts` — remove import + completion call block
- `src/commands/close.ts` — remove import + three close-path call blocks + recovery comment
- `packages/shared/src/types.ts` — remove `openBrainEnabled` from `WorklogConfig`
- `.worklog/config.yaml` — remove `openBrainEnabled: true`
- `tests/unit/openbrain.test.ts` — delete
- `tests/cli/openbrain-close.test.ts` — delete
- `docs/openbrain.md` — delete
- `docs/feature-requests/openbrain-playwright-fallback-retrieval.md` — delete (OpenBrain feature request; would fail AC3 repo-wide search)
- `CLI.md`, `README.md` — remove OpenBrain references

## Related work

- WL-0MNM4SDMA000GOBC — "Whenever a work item is marked as completed/done update OpenBrain": introduced the integration (predecessor).
- WL-0MOHP1FIP007LYCB — "Make wl close OpenBrain submission fully non-blocking": changed the close flow (predecessor).
- WL-0MNRPS89H004COB0 — "Fix validator and openbrain test failures": fixed CLI.md docs + EPIPE handling (predecessor).
- WL-0MRTSOK8C009CDLA — "Process lifecycle utility module": references `src/openbrain.ts` as a spawn user; the process-lifecycle/spawn helpers themselves must be preserved.
- WL-0MQP4RDG2006LFM9 — ruff lint fix whose description matched `docs/openbrain.md` (search-index noise only).

## Effort and Risk

- Effort: **S** — deletions plus a handful of targeted edits; rebuild required.
- Risk: **Low** — opt-in flag; no other project enables it; `ob` unavailable so no live dependents. Residual risks: missed references (mitigated by the AC3 repo-wide search) and stale built `dist/` (mitigated by the rebuild in Desired change / AC5).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1** (Map/intake, 2026-09-19): "Should 'Remove openbrain' mean (A) remove the integration from the shared `worklog` codebase (~600 lines), or (B) only disable it in this project's `.worklog/config.yaml` (one line)? The title points at (A), the description ('in this project, but not any other … disable it') at (B). Reply A, B, or both."
  - **Answer (producer): "Both"** — do (A) **and** (B): remove the feature from the shared codebase AND remove the `openBrainEnabled: true` line from `.worklog/config.yaml`. Source: producer reply to comment WL-C0MU89PEMR004ISDS on WL-0MTH28WDS008WMXA.
data.title: Remove openbrain

# Pawn shop should reduce, not increase reputation (WL-0MTH6B20C002ZOM2) — Intake brief

## Problem statement

The Pawn Shop business card (`biz-pawnshop`, Main Street game, `Tableau-Card-Engine`) is currently **increasing** the player's reputation by +5 per turn and costs 300 coins to purchase — both incorrect per design intent. A pawn shop should be a low-reputation, budget-friendly establishment: it should **reduce** reputation by 0.1 per turn and be cheaper to acquire (200 coins at the ×100 scale, i.e. 2.00 in game terms).

## Users (example user stories)

- **As a player**, I expect placing a Pawn Shop on my street to slightly harm my reputation each turn (`-0.1`), not boost it, so that reputation decisions involve meaningful trade-offs.
- **As a player**, I expect the Pawn Shop to remain an accessible budget business (cheaper than the 300-coin tier-2 group) despite its per-turn reputation penalty.
- **As a maintainer**, I expect CSV card data and tests to stay internally consistent (numeric columns valid; ongoing-cost convention preserved).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Negative reputation per turn.** `biz-pawnshop.reputationPerTurn` in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` changes from `5` to `-0.1`; placing the Pawn Shop on the street grid accrues a **negative** reputation delta (−0.1) during the income phase (`applyIncome`), never a positive one.
2. **Reduced purchase cost.** `biz-pawnshop.cost` in the CSV changes from `300` to `200`; the market purchase price for the Pawn Shop is 200 (2.00 at the ×100 display convention).
3. **Synergy opt-out unchanged.** The Pawn Shop still provides and receives **zero** synergy bonuses (`synergyCoinBonus = 0`, `synergyRepBonus = 0`, no adjacency synergy) — unchanged behaviour (existing tests in `adjacency.test.ts` / `MainStreetHandSynergy.test.ts` still pass).
4. **Test coverage.** Add or extend automated tests asserting (a) the Pawn Shop's negative per-turn reputation and (b) its updated cost of 200; the full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
5. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (card tooltips/descriptions generated from CSV, `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` and any README/wikis as applicable, including code comments). Note: `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- CSV numeric columns are validated by `src/balance-cards/csv.ts` (`parseFloat`); `-0.1` is a valid numeric value.
- Costs use the ×100 integer convention (200 = 2.00 coins); `reputationPerTurn` is applied raw at income time (no ×100) — confirm via tests during implementation.
- **Do not** regenerate costs via the balance-cards curve tool (`src/balance-cards/algorithm.ts`): it would reassign tier bands. Its Pawn Shop special case (cost −2) applies only when `baseIncome === 0`, which is not our case — no algorithm change needed.
- Ongoing-cost convention (documented in `tests/main-street/business-ongoing-cost.test.ts`) is `max(25, cost / 4)`. **Assumption (producer to confirm):** if `cost` becomes 200, `ongoingCost` follows the convention to 50 (currently 75). The producer's clarification specified only the purchase cost; do not change `ongoingCost` unless confirmed.

## Existing state

Current `biz-pawnshop` row in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv`:

```

```

## Desired change

| `reputationPerTurn` | `5` | `-0.1` (reduces reputation 0.1/turn) |
| `cost` | `300` | `200` (2.00 at ×100) |

## Risks & assumptions

# Intake Brief — Boost audit-backed items in wl next sorting (WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5)

## Problem statement

`wl next` and the automatic `reSort` scoring currently rank work without considering whether an audit has been performed. An audit that is `not ready to close` signals that substantive work has been done and the item needs iteration, yet those items compete equally with untouched items that have never been audited. This causes nearly-complete work to slip behind fresh untouched items (of equal or higher base priority), delaying iteration. A deliberate boost for audit-backed, not-ready-to-close items — second only to `critical` priority — is needed.

## Users

- **Developers using `wl next` / Pi TUI selection list** who pick the next item to work on.
  - *As a developer, when I have audited an item and it is not yet ready to close, I want it to appear ahead of any unaudited non-critical item in `wl next`, so iteration on in-progress work is prioritized over starting new untouched work.*
- **Producers / reviewers triaging `wl next -n N`** who scan the grouped list for next actions.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Audit-not-ready boost in scoring:** Items that have an `audit_results` row with `ready_to_close = false` receive a score boost during `reSort`/`computeScore` (and any equivalent ordering path) such that, after `wl re-sort` or auto `reSort` triggered by `wl next`, every non-critical audited-not-ready item is ordered before every unaudited (or audit-ready-to-close) non-critical item, regardless of base priority (high/medium/low) and regardless of age/effort/recency tie-breakers. `critical` items remain strictly ahead of audited-not-ready items even if unaudited.
2. **No boost for ready-to-close or missing audit:** Items with no audit row, or with `ready_to_close = true`, receive no audit boost and retain their existing score. Stale audits (where `auditedAt < updatedAt`) are treated as not boosted — only a fresh audit (`auditedAt >= updatedAt`) that is not ready counts — unless explicitly decided otherwise during implementation (document the chosen freshness rule).
3. **`wl next` reflects the boosted order:** `wl next -n N` (with and without `--no-re-sort`) returns items in the same boosted order; `wl next --json` preserves the order; when all `sortIndex` values are equal the fallback `selectBySortIndex` tie-break also respects the audit boost before falling back to effective priority/age.
4. **Critical exemption preserved:** No non-critical item, even with an audit-not-ready boost, outranks a `critical` priority item. The existing Critical Group ordering in `src/commands/grouping.ts` / `packages/shared` remains unchanged.
5. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes (including existing `reSort` and `findNextWorkItem` tests).
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README/CLI docs, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Only `ready_to_close = false` audits qualify; `true` or absent audits do not boost.
- `critical` priority is never overtaken by the audit boost (hard tier boundary).
- No new external dependencies; change is confined to scoring/sorting logic.
- Must not regress performance of `wl next` or `reSort` on large datasets; audit lookups should use existing `getAuditResult` / cached maps, not per-item N+1 queries without caching.
- Backward compatible: no CLI flag changes required; existing `wl next` flags continue to work.

## Existing state

- **`packages/shared/src/database.ts:computeScore()` / `sortItemsByScore()` / `reSort()`** — Score drives `sortIndex` via `getAllOrderedByScore()`. Weights: priority 1000, in_review 600, blocks-high-priority 500, etc. No audit awareness.
- **`packages/shared/src/database.ts:findNextWorkItemFromItems()` / `selectBySortIndex()`** — Selection uses `sortIndex` order; when all `sortIndex` equal, falls back to effective priority then `createdAt`. No audit tie-break.
- **`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` / `audit_results` table** — `saveAuditResult`, `getAuditResult`, `getAllAuditResults`. `wl next` already enriches items with `auditResult` for display but does not use it for ordering.
- **`src/commands/grouping.ts:assignItemGroups()`** — Critical items in `Critical Group N`; remaining groups by stage/file-path. Audit does not affect grouping (by design).
- **TUI selection list** consumes `wl next --json` ordering; boosting `computeScore` automatically benefits the TUI.

## Desired change

1. Extend `computeScore()` (and the parallel `selectBySortIndex` fallback path, if needed) to apply an **audit-not-ready boost** when `store.getAuditResult(id)` (or a batch-fetched map / `EdgeCache`-style cache) returns `readyToClose === false` and the audit is fresh (`auditedAt >= updatedAt`). The boost must be large enough to outrank any non-critical base priority difference (e.g., tiered comparison or numeric boost > 2000 so `low` + boost > `high` unaudited). Keep `critical` (4000) strictly above `high`+boost.
2. Thread the audit freshness check through `sortItemsByScore` / `getAllOrderedByScore` efficiently (batch map, not per-item uncached query in the hot loop).
3. Ensure `findNextWorkItemFromItems` fallback ordering also respects the same audit tier when `sortIndex` values are uniform.
4. Add/adjust unit tests for `database.test.ts` / `persistent-store` covering: audited-not-ready outranks unaudited high, critical outranks audited, ready-to-close gets no boost, missing audit gets no boost, stale audit handling.
5. Update docs/comments (`docs/`, `CLI.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` if needed) to describe the new audit boost tier.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `computeScore()`, `sortItemsByScore()`, `getAllOrderedByScore()`, `reSort()`, `findNextWorkItemFromItems()`, `selectBySortIndex()`.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — `audit_results` table helpers (`getAuditResult`, `getAllAuditResults`) for efficient audit lookup.
- `src/commands/grouping.ts` — Verify no grouping change needed; critical tier stays top (reference only).
- `src/commands/next.ts` — Enriches `auditResult` for display; ordering comes from DB layer (reference).
- `tests/database.test.ts` (and `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts` if present) — Add reSort/next ordering tests for audit boost.

## Related work

- **WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5** — This item (audit boost).
- **`packages/shared/src/database.ts:computeScore` weights** — Existing priority/in_review/blocks-high-priority scoring to be extended.
- **`audit_results` table (WL-0MPZNJVWT000IKG7)** — Sole source of truth for audit state; `wl next` already displays audit icons via this table.
- **Critical Group feature (`src/commands/grouping.ts`)** — Establishes precedent for a hard tier (critical) that must remain above the new audit tier.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Boost magnitude risk:** A modest numeric boost (e.g., +600 like in_review) would not outrank a higher priority unaudited item, violating "ahead of any non-critical unaudited". **Mitigation:** Implement as tiered comparison (audit-not-ready tier outranks unaudited tier) or numeric boost > max priority delta (>2000) and cover with tests.
- **Stale audit risk:** Audits older than the work item's `updatedAt` may no longer reflect current work. **Assumption:** Only fresh audits (`auditedAt >= updatedAt`) qualify for the boost; stale audits are treated as no-audit. Record final decision in implementation and document it. If the producer prefers stale audits to still boost, adjust before implementation.
- **Performance risk:** Per-item `getAuditResult` in the sort comparator could be N+1. **Mitigation:** Build a `Map<id, AuditResult>` once per `sortItemsByScore` / `reSort` call and reuse, mirroring `EdgeCache` pattern.
- **Scope creep:** Requests for configurable boost, per-priority audit tiers, or grouping changes. **Mitigation:** File separate work items; keep this item to a single audit-not-ready tier second only to critical.
- **Assumption:** `ready_to_close = true` items are typically `in_review` and already receive an in_review boost; they should not receive the additional audit-not-ready boost.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should an audit with `ready_to_close = true` also receive the boost, or only `false`? — Answer (seed intent): Only `not ready to close` (false) should be boosted — ready items are already terminal/in_review and do not need iteration priority. Source: work-item description ("have an audit on file but that are not ready to close").
- Q: Should `critical` items be overtaken by a lower-priority audited item? — Answer (seed intent): No — "ahead of any item (other than critical) that have no audit" implies critical remains on top regardless of audit. Source: work-item description.
- Q: Should stale audits (`auditedAt < updatedAt`) still count for the boost? — Answer (assumption, to be confirmed in implementation): No — only fresh audits (`auditedAt >= updatedAt`) qualify; stale audits are treated as no audit for ordering. Rationale: edited work invalidates prior audit signal. Open to producer override; will document final rule in code comments.
- Q: Is the boost a hard tier (any audited-not-ready outranks any unaudited non-critical) or a modest priority-relative nudge? — Answer (seed intent): Hard tier — "ahead of any item (other than critical) that have no audit" indicates tier, not relative nudge. Final: implement as tiered ordering (or equivalent large numeric boost >2000).

## Goal

Fix the freshness clock so that post-audit comments do not invalidate audits.

## Problem

`wl comment add` calls `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt()` which updates `updatedAt`.
The `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` check in icons.ts returns false when
`auditedAt <= updatedAt - 60s`, so a comment added after the audit makes it
appear stale.

## Proposed solution

Option (c) - atomic audit persistence: `wl audit-set` (and `wl update --audit-text`)
should atomically set `updatedAt = auditedAt` (or `updatedAt >= auditedAt`) when
recording an audit. This ensures that immediately after an audit, the freshness
check always passes, regardless of subsequent comments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl audit-set` sets updatedAt = auditedAt (or later) atomically with the audit record
- [ ] `wl update --audit-text` path behaves identically
- [ ] After audit, `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` returns true immediately
- [ ] No race window where a read between audit-set and display sees stale data

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` - `saveAuditResult` method
- `src/commands/audit-result.ts` - `wl audit-set` command
- `src/commands/update.ts` - `wl update --audit-text` command
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` - `isAuditFresh` function

# Sprint Complete: Auto-Disable Dispatch & Ship Banner

## Problem statement

When all work items in the current sprint have been completed or reviewed (i.e., completed/in_review count >= the browseItemCount setting), the herdr extension should automatically disable downtime dispatching and display a green banner prompting the operator to ship.

## Users

- **Sprint lead / operator**: Sees a clear visual signal when the sprint is done and knows they can ship.
- **Downtime worker**: Stops wasting compute resources dispatching work when there's nothing left to do.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Auto-disable dispatch**: When `completed + in_review` item count >= `browseItemCount` setting, the downtime worker automatically disables dispatching (writes the disable marker, same mechanism as the `d` shortcut).
2. **Green sprint-complete banner**: A green-background, white-text banner replaces the help text below the item list displaying: `Sprint Complete, hit S to ship`.
3. **Re-enable on new items**: When new work items arrive (completed/in_review count drops below `browseItemCount`), the disable marker is removed and the banner disappears, restoring normal behavior.
4. **Banner only when sprint complete**: The sprint-complete banner is shown ONLY when the condition is met AND the help text is enabled (`showHelpText: true`); it does not interfere with code-freeze banners.
5. **All tests pass**: Full project test suite passes with new changes.
6. **Related documentation updated**: Code comments and any relevant docs reflect the new behavior.

## Constraints

- **Fail-closed**: If the item count query fails, default to NOT auto-disabling (conservative).
- **Non-blocking**: The auto-disable must not crash the TUI or block normal operation.
- **Marker reuse**: Use the existing `.herdr-downtime-disabled` marker file mechanism — no new persistence mechanism.
- **Banner placement**: Banner replaces the help text footer area (same chrome row budget accounting as code-freeze banners).

## Existing state

- The `browseItemCount` setting (default 20) controls how many items are displayed.
- The downtime worker already has a disable-marker mechanism (`.herdr-downtime-disabled`) used by the `d` shortcut.
- Code-freeze banners already render above the item list with proper chrome row accounting.
- The help text footer is rendered below the list and is gated by `showHelpText`.
- Completed/in_review items are tracked via `wl list --status completed --stage in_review`.

## Desired change

- Add a completion-check hook that runs on each list refresh and worker tick.
- When the completion condition is met: write the disable marker, suppress the help text footer, and render the green banner.
- When the condition clears: remove the disable marker, restore the help text, and remove the banner.
- The banner text includes "hit S to ship" referencing the existing `S` shortcut for ship confirmation (WL-0MSGG5N5Z0074TLY).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Add completion check logic to the worker tick loop; wire auto-disable into the existing marker mechanism.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Add `sprintComplete` boolean parameter to the renderer; render green banner in place of help text when active.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-disable-marker.ts` — Reuse existing marker write/remove functions; add a `sprintCompleteMarkerExists` check if needed.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — Add `fetchCompletedItemCount()` helper to count completed/in_review items.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — No changes needed (uses existing `browseItemCount`).

## Related work

- Code-freeze banners: `WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY` — similar banner rendering pattern.
- Disable marker: `WL-0MT4BWUHW008LIFE` — existing `.herdr-downtime-disabled` mechanism.
- Ship confirmation dialog: `WL-0MSGG5N5Z0074TLY` — the `S` shortcut the banner references.

# Intake Draft — Downtime dispatcher: exclude items needing producer review from selection

**Work item:** WL-0MTIAL65N004T22F

## Problem statement

The herdr downtime dispatcher auto-dispatches the next eligible work item during idle LLM slots, but it currently ignores the `needsProducerReview` flag. Items flagged `needsProducerReview=true` are awaiting a human producer decision and should not be auto-worked; dispatching them wastes local slots, conflicts with the review gate, and can trigger work the producer explicitly paused.

## Users

- **Herdr operators** running `packages/herdr` downtime dispatch in local-model idle periods.
- **Producers** who set `needsProducerReview` to gate an item until human review completes.

User stories:
- "As an operator, I want downtime dispatch to skip items awaiting producer review so idle slots are spent on actionable work."
- "As a producer, I want flagging an item for review to immediately remove it from the downtime queue so it is not auto-started while I review it."

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Downtime dispatch never selects an item with `needsProducerReview === true` as a candidate, across every tier: audit (`completed`/`in_review` without valid audit), implement (`plan_complete` with risk/effort caps), critical-first (critical across stages, including frontier blockers), `intake_complete` → `/skill:plan`, and `idea` → `/skill:intake`. Items with `needsProducerReview === false` or absent/undefined remain dispatchable.
- AC2: The critical-frontier resolver also excludes `needsProducerReview=true` blockers: if the highest-priority critical candidate is blocked only by review-gated blockers (or the critical item itself needs review), the tier returns no candidate and falls through to the next tier.
- AC3: Coordination (leader) path is equally gated: the leader's per-entry fetch/classification (`fetchItem` + tier mapping) skips entries whose current item has `needsProducerReview === true`; the offer list retains the entry for later re-offer after the flag is cleared, and dispatch falls through to the next dispatchable entry.
- AC4: Filtering is fail-safe at every boundary: a missing/unparseable `needsProducerReview` field is treated as `false` (dispatchable); a malformed item never crashes dispatch and never disables a tier.
- AC5: Regression tests cover the exclusion per tier (unit + `downtime-worker`/`index` level) and verify that clearing the flag makes the item dispatchable again; existing herdr and project test suites pass.
- AC6: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- AC7: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Change is confined to the dispatch selection path; do not change the meaning of `needsProducerReview` elsewhere (TUI filters, `wl list --needs-producer-review`, status lifecycle remain unchanged).
- Fail-closed/fail-safe per tier: a filtering error must not crash the worker and must not silently disable an entire tier; follow the existing `DowntimeNextResult` / null-fallback error channels.
- Do not introduce a new `wl next` CLI flag if client-side filtering in the downtime deps suffices and keeps the change minimal; if a server-side filter is added, it must remain backward compatible.
- Preserve existing dispatched-marker, code-freeze, audit-freshness, and active-audit single-flight guards.

## Existing state

- Dispatcher tiers in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` + `packages/herdr/src/index.ts: createDowntimeDeps()`:
  - `getNextAuditCandidate` → `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only` → `selectAuditCandidate`
  - `getNextImplementCandidate` → `wl next --stage plan_complete --risk medium --effort medium -n 10` → `selectImplementCandidate`
  - `getNextItem('intake_complete'/'idea')` → `wl next --stage <stage> -n 10` → `selectNextCandidate` (with plan/intake dispatched-marker change-guard)
  - `getNextCriticalCandidate` → `wl list --priority critical --status open -n 10` → `selectCriticalCandidate` + `resolveDependencyFrontier`
  - Leader coordination path: `dispatchFromCoordination` iterates the durable offer list, `fetchItem` (`wl show` enriched) per entry, tier classification, shared `recordDispatch`/`spawnAgentPane` path.
- None of these filters currently check `needsProducerReview`; `wl list`/`wl next` server-side can filter by `needsProducerReview` (persistent-store `AND workitems.needsProducerReview = ?`) but the downtime deps do not pass it. Client-side `WorkItem.needsProducerReview` is available on every fetched item (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts: normalizeItem`).
- `needsProducerReview` is a tri-state integer → boolean (0/1, default 0) stored in `workitems` and surfaced via `wl list --needs-producer-review`.

## Desired change

- Filter `needsProducerReview === true` items out of every downtime selection path, client-side in the downtime deps (and, if justified, server-side via `--needs-producer-review false` on the `wl` queries):
  - `getNextAuditCandidate`, `getNextImplementCandidate`, `getNextItem`, `getNextCriticalCandidate` exclude review-gated candidates before `select*` (and re-check frontier blockers for critical).
  - Coordination leader path: `fetchItem` result with `needsProducerReview true` is skipped (not a dispatchable tier match) and the loop continues to the next offer entry.
- Treat `needsProducerReview` absent/null as dispatchable (explicit `=== true` check only).
- Add/extend tests in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` and `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` (and `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` for the leader path) covering: per-tier exclusion, frontier exclusion, leader skip, and flag-clear → dispatchable.
- Update downtime-worker header comment and inline tier comments to document the review-gate exclusion.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `createDowntimeDeps`: `getNextItem`, `getNextAuditCandidate`, `getNextImplementCandidate`, `getNextCriticalCandidate`, `fetchItem` wiring; where `needsProducerReview` filtering is added.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — tier orchestration (`dispatchDowntimeWork`, `dispatchFromCoordination`), header contract, per-tier selection helpers; docs + leader-loop handling.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.ts` — leader dispatch loop iterating the offer list (if separate from downtime-worker; otherwise within `downtime-worker.ts`).
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` / `src/persistent-store.ts` — server-side `needsProducerReview` filter (`AND workitems.needsProducerReview = ?`) if a CLI flag is passed through.
- `src/commands/next.ts` / `src/commands/list.ts` — `wl` CLI surface for `--needs-producer-review` if server-side filtering is used.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `WorkItem.needsProducerReview` normalization (already present; verify shape used by filters).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — regression tests for the new gate.

## Related work

- WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG — audit tier (completed/in_review without valid audit) — dispatch tier filtered here.
- WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6 — implement tier end-to-end (plan_complete risk/effort caps) — dispatch tier filtered here.
- WL-0MT3FM8VA005XBHE — critical items always progress first regardless of stage — critical-first tier + frontier resolver filtered here.
- WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY — dispatched-marker exclusion in audit-tier selection — existing selection-exclusion pattern this change follows.
- WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT — downtime dispatched-marker change-guard (RCA) — existing plan/intake exclusion pattern.
- WL-0MLGTWT4S1X4HDD9 / WL-0MLGTKW490NJTOAB — `--needs-producer-review` filter and Needs Producer Review flag — storage/query capability reused.
- WL-0MSN6Z9HN00637XY — flipping needsProducerReview must not make a valid audit stale — adjacent invariant to preserve.
- WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7 / WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL — coordination (leader offer list) path — leader per-entry classification filtered here.

Automated find_related report: see `find_related` step output persisted to `.worklog/tmp/` (if generated).

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: `needsProducerReview === true` means "human must act first — do not auto-dispatch for any skill (audit/implement/plan/intake)". If some tier should still dispatch (e.g. audit while awaiting review), that would need a separate follow-up item — ask rather than expanding scope.
- Assumption: filtering is `=== true` only; absent/false/undefined items are dispatchable. No tri-state "unknown = blocked" interpretation.
- Assumption: when every candidate in a tier needs review, the tier reports "no candidate" (not a `wl-error` strike) and dispatch falls through exactly as an empty backlog does — no cooldown triggered.
- Risk: adding filtering at both server and client layers could double-filter or mask errors; prefer client-side filtering first and add server-side flag only if it eliminates a meaningful batch-starvation window (batch is already `-n 10`).
- Risk: leader offer list could starve if every offered entry needs review — the leader must fall through gracefully and not pause with a no-candidate cooldown while review-gated items exist.
- Scope-creep risk: extending the flag's semantics (e.g., auto-clearing on review, new `wl next --needs-producer-review` default) is out of scope — record as separate work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should downtime dispatch skip items needing producer review? — Answer (operator): Yes — "When the downtime dispatcher selecting next issues to work on do not select work items marked as needing producer review." Source: intake seed text (`/intake` argument).
- Q: Which tiers does this apply to? — Answer (assumption documented, no question asked): All dispatch tiers (audit, implement, critical-first, plan, intake) and the coordination leader path. Reasonable default: review-gated items should not be auto-worked at any tier. Source: inferred from seed ("selecting next issues to work on" = all selection).
- Q: How does a flagged item become dispatchable again? — Answer (assumption documented, no question asked): Clearing the flag (`wl update <id> --needs-producer-review false`) makes it eligible again; the next idle poll may then select it. Source: existing flag semantics, no change to lifecycle.

# Herdr selection list requires double dispatch for priority update to reflect (WL-0MTIB7JAN004MQ8N)

## Problem statement

Running a chord command in the Herdr selection list that updates priority (e.g. `u p c` → `!!wl update <id> --priority critical`) appears to require sending the command twice before the display reflects the new priority. It is unclear whether the first `wl update` fails to execute or whether it succeeds but the list refresh renders stale data. The bug degrades trust in the selection list — operators cannot tell if their update was applied.

## Users

- **Herdr TUI operators** browsing and triaging work items via `packages/herdr`.
  - *As a Herdr user, I want `u p c` (and sibling priority chords `u p l/m/h`) to update the displayed priority immediately after the command completes, so I know the change was applied without needing to re-issue the command.*
- **Downtime / maintenance operators** who use chord shortcuts for rapid triage.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Single dispatch, visible update**: After pressing `u p c` (or `u p l`, `u p m`, `u p h`) on a selected item, the selection list shows the updated priority after the underlying `wl update` completes — without requiring a second dispatch or manual `r` refresh.
2. **No premature stale fetch**: The list does not fetch/display stale data that races ahead of the background `wl update`. At least one refresh is guaranteed to occur *after* the `wl update` child process exits.
3. **Single-flight guard does not drop the post-completion refresh**: If an immediate refresh is in-flight when the background shell exits, the post-exit refresh is not silently skipped; it is coalesced/trailing-scheduled and runs after the in-flight fetch completes.
4. **All `open_pane: false` modifying shortcuts behave the same**: The fix applies consistently to `u p *`, `a y`/`a r` (audit), and any other `!!wl` background chords that use `onExit → onRefresh` (no per-chord special case).
5. **No regression for visible-pane / filter shortcuts**: `/wl --priority`, `/wl <stage>` filter chords and agent-skill chords (`/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`) continue to refresh/behave as before.
6. **Tests validate the fix**: New or updated tests assert (a) background modifying chord dispatch does not trigger an immediate stale fetch that blocks the trailing refresh, (b) `doRefresh` coalescing/trailing behaviour, and (c) priority update reflected after background exit.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.
8. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md` or docs where chord refresh is described, and any relevant inline docs.

## Constraints

- **No change to `shortcuts.json` command strings** — the `!!wl update <id> --priority …` commands and `open_pane: false` remain as-is.
- The fix must preserve the detached/background execution model (`spawnBackgroundShell` with `detached: true` + `unref()` + `onExit` refresh) — do not switch `u p *` back to a visible pane.
- `refreshInFlight` single-flight protection must remain (prevents wl spawn storms), but must not silently drop a trailing refresh.
- Minimal surface area: prefer a change scoped to `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` and/or `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`; do not redesign `fetcher.ts` timeouts unless necessary.

## Existing state

- `shortcuts.json` defines `u p l/m/h/c` as `!!wl update <id> --priority …` with `"open_pane": false`.
- `worklist.ts:dispatchChordCommand` routes `!!wl update|close|delete|search` through `resolveAndRouteCommand` so `executeResolvedCommand` returns `'dispatched'` (WL-0MTA217DZ003H5K8).
- `worklist.ts:onData` (chord-complete and single-key paths) does `if (result === 'dispatched' && isWlModifyingCommand(command)) await doRefresh(true)` — an **immediate** refresh that races with the background `wl update`.
- `index.ts:onCommand` for `route === 'pane'` with `openPane === false` spawns via `spawnBackgroundShell(clean, …, { onExit: () => onRefresh?.() })` where `onRefresh = () => doRefresh(false)`.
- `worklist.ts:doRefresh` has a single-flight guard `if (refreshInFlight) return;` with no coalescing — a second `doRefresh` that fires while the first is awaiting `fetchItemsForView` is silently dropped. `fetchItemsForView` duration (~100–300 ms) overlaps with `wl update` duration, so the `onExit` refresh is frequently dropped and the list stays stale until the next manual/timer refresh or a second dispatch.
- Duplicate report exists: WL-0MTFRJ2V6005IMW1 ("Update Priority in selection list does not instantly update the list").

## Desired change

1. **Suppress premature immediate refresh for background dispatches** — in both chord-complete and single-key dispatch paths, skip `await doRefresh(true)` when `openPane === false` (background). The post-exit `onRefresh` is the correct freshness point for these commands.
2. **Make `doRefresh` trailing/coalescing** — when `refreshInFlight` is true, record that a trailing refresh was requested and run it after the current fetch completes (one trailing run, not unbounded queuing). This guarantees the `onExit` refresh is not lost even if other refreshes are in-flight.
3. **Alternatively** (if (1) alone is deemed insufficient): keep immediate refresh but ensure it is not racy — e.g. delay the immediate fetch until after a short grace or make the background spawn synchronous for data-modifying chords. The implementer should evaluate (1)+(2) as the primary approach and document the decision.
4. **Add targeted tests** in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` and/or `worklist-inflight.test.ts` that simulate the race (immediate + onExit overlapping) and assert the list ends in fresh state.
5. **Ensure `isWlModifyingCommand` / `dispatchChordCommand` remain consistent** — no new command families; the regex `/^!!\s*wl\s+(close|delete|update|reviewed|search)\b/i` already covers `u p *`.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Chord dispatch paths (`executeResolvedCommand` → `isWlModifyingCommand` immediate `doRefresh`), `doRefresh` single-flight guard, `ChordState.resolvedOpenPane` plumbing.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `onCommand` background route (`spawnBackgroundShell` + `onExit: () => onRefresh?.()`), `spawnBackgroundShell` / `spawnBackgroundPi` helpers.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — `u p l/m/h/c` entries (`open_pane: false`); not expected to change but contexts the bug.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchItemsForView` / `fetchNextItems` timing (context for race window).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-inflight.test.ts` — Existing single-flight tests; extend for trailing/coalescing case.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Integration / chord dispatch tests.

## Related work

- **WL-0MTFRJ2V6005IMW1** — "Update Priority in selection list does not instantly update the list" (open, medium). Direct duplicate/narrower report of the same symptom for `u p` commands.
- **WL-0MTA217DZ003H5K8** — "Fix shortcut commands not refreshing selection list" (completed, high). Prior fix that routed `!!wl close/delete/update/search` through `dispatchChordCommand` so `isWlModifyingCommand` triggers an immediate refresh. This item's immediate-refresh strategy introduced/raced with the background `onExit` refresh, which this bug addresses.
- **WL-0MT26TE72002FLKX** — "counts in Herdr selection list are incorrect" (open, high). Possibly related stale-fetch symptom.
- **WL-0MSBVBNGH002RDP5** — "momentary collapse" flicker fix (atomic fetch of expanded children) — context for `doRefresh` fetch sequencing.
- **WL-0MSBVYBMD004007C** — Introduced `refreshInFlight` single-flight guard — the guard whose non-coalescing behavior contributes to the dropped trailing refresh.
- **WL-0MSJLD1I70045ZUL** — Introduced `open_pane: false` background execution (`spawnBackgroundShell`/`spawnBackgroundPi` + `onRefresh` hook).
- **WL-0MT1KB70U0012X6T** — Wired completion-triggered refresh hook (`onRefresh` via `onExit`) for background dispatches.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — primary files to change.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: `wl update <id> --priority …` always succeeds quickly (<500 ms); the bug is a refresh timing/race, not a `wl` failure. If `wl update` itself fails silently, the refresh will still show stale data — out of scope for this item (requires separate error surfacing).
- **Assumption**: `spawnBackgroundShell`'s `ChildProcess 'exit'` event reliably fires for detached `bash -c "wl …"` children while the parent TUI is still running. If it does not, the trailing refresh never runs — verify with a manual test and consider a fallback timer-based refresh if needed.
- **Risk: Over-coalescing causes extra refresh storms** — Mitigation: trailing refresh is at-most-once per in-flight cycle, not unbounded queuing.
- **Risk: Suppressing immediate refresh for background chords hides feedback** — Mitigation: the `Sent` toast still fires immediately; only the data fetch is deferred to `onExit`; add a short-lived "Updating…" indicator if needed (defer to follow-up item if out of scope).
- **Scope-creep risk**: Generalizing the fix to all command types or redesigning the fetcher timeout/background log system. Mitigation: keep scope to `doRefresh` coalescing + conditional immediate refresh for `openPane === false`; record broader improvements as separate work items linked to this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is the `wl update` actually executed on the first chord invocation, or does the chord dispatch itself fail?" — Answer: Not yet verified; to be confirmed during implementation by inspecting the per-run background log (`herdr-background-logs/herdr-*.log`) and the `wl` DB after a single `u p c`. The intake hypothesis is that the command *does* execute but the subsequent refresh is stale/raced. Source: this intake analysis — requires implementer to verify.
- Q: "Should the fix suppress the immediate refresh for background modifying commands, make `doRefresh` coalescing, or both?" — Answer: Recommended to do both — suppress immediate for `openPane === false` (no premature fetch) *and* make `doRefresh` trailing so an overlapping `onExit` refresh is never dropped. The implementer should validate and document the final choice. Source: analysis of `worklist.ts:doRefresh` and `index.ts:spawnBackgroundShell` interaction.
- Q: "Does this duplicate WL-0MTFRJ2V6005IMW1?" — Answer: Yes, WL-0MTFRJ2V6005IMW1 reports the same symptom narrowly for `u p`. Propose linking as duplicate/blocked-by and closing the older on completion of this item, keeping this as the canonical critical bug. Source: `wl search` and `wl show` inspection.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSRWJRQ1003NX4U** – test skill: node_suite_commands() ignores detected project root (vacuous node suite for non-framework repos) (open)
- **WL-0MLCX6PK41VWGPRE** – Optimize issue update API calls in wl github push (completed)
- **WL-0MT3IA41F0074CWN** – Docs & observability for critical-first tier (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: always, clear, command, critical, dispatch, display, double, first, herdr, list, priority, reflect, requires, run, running, selection, sent, time, update, updates, when
- `CLI.md` — matched: always, clear, command, critical, display, first, herdr, list, priority, reflect, requires, run, running, selection, sent, time, update, updates, when
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: always, command, critical, dispatch, display, first, herdr, list, priority, requires, run, selection, sent, time, twice, update, updates, when

> Automated report: weak signal — the substantive related work is the curated list above (WL-0MTFRJ2V6005IMW1 duplicate, WL-0MTA217DZ003H5K8, WL-0MSJLD1I70045ZUL, etc.).

# Machine coordination dir resolver

# Shared coordination file (machine-wide)

## Summary
Move coordination.json and its lock to the machine dir; entries carry worklogRoot so all instances read/write the same file. Retain tmp+rename atomic write, O_CREAT|O_EXCL lock, and stale-entry pruning.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] One shared coordination dir: A second herdr instance opened on a *different* worklog joins the same coordination file; the file contains entries with different `worklogRoot`s. — headless test with two temp worklog roots proves shared file (covers parent AC1)
- [ ] Fail-safe: unreadable/corrupt coordination file returns null and the tick skips dispatch (never throws or drops another instance's entry)
- [ ] Lock serializes concurrent read-modify-write; atomic tmp+rename prevents half-written JSON
- [ ] worklogRoot field is the worklog root (parent of .worklog), backward compat with legacy directory field; build green

- Rename/retain directory -> worklogRoot (keep directory as alias for compat); entries {instanceId, workItemId, worklogRoot/directory, assignedAt, lastUpdated}
- Update pruneStaleEntries to run against machine file
- Headless test packages/herdr/tests/coordination-machine.test.ts

- Updated coordination.ts + headless test + code comments

# Single machine-wide leader election

## Summary
Point leader-election lock and 5-min lease at the machine dir — one election, one lease machine-wide. Reuse ownership-based refreshLease() and per-tick re-derivation (zombie-safe WL-0MTEZ5EK5002RXXD). Wire through createDowntimeWorker (remove per-worklog join(targetCwd,'.worklog') coupling).

# Intake Brief: Fair round-robin work scheduling with priority override (WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V)

## Problem Statement
The `dispatchFromCoordination` leader path in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` selects from the shared coordination file (`downtime-coordination.json`) by iterating entries in file order within each tier. With multiple projects contributing (ContextHub, SorraAgents, AI_Hell, Tableau-Card-Engine), this allows the same project to monopolise consecutive dispatch slots. We need globally-fair distribution with an exception for critical-priority items.

## Users

- **Agent — Automated downtime worker (primary):** As a downtime worker I want dispatches to fairly represent all contributing projects, so that no single project starves others of agent attention.
- **Developer / Project owner:** As a developer with work in an unserved project, I want the scheduler to eventually assign my project's candidate even when another project has more frequent offers, so that my backlog makes progress.

### User Stories
- As the downtime dispatcher leader, when entries exist from multiple projects at the same tier, I select the project whose last dispatch (in any tier) is oldest (round-robin), so that projects get a fair share of slots.
- As a project owner with a `critical`-priority offer on file, my next dispatch should bypass round-robin and run immediately (still at its stage-appropriate skill), so that urgent work is not delayed by fairness.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `dispatchFromCoordination` selects across the shared coordination entries in **global cross-project round-robin** order: among equally-eligible (tier-matched, non-critical) entries, the project whose `worklogRoot` was least-recently dispatched (with persistence across leader restarts / cycles) is chosen first. New / unknown roots sort first (never penalised). A single persistent cursor/state per worklog root (e.g. in a JSON file alongside the coordination file) drives the ordering; concurrent leaders do not corrupt the cursor (fail-open).
- [ ] When **any** entry on file is a `critical`-priority open item at a dispatchable stage (`idea` / `intake_complete` / `plan_complete` within caps; stage-appropriate skill), the leader dispatches that critical entry **immediately** ahead of all non-critical entries, regardless of round-robin position. Within the critical subset, selection remains deterministic (existing priority/sortIndex tie-break — one item per project, so round-robin is not needed inside critical).
- [ ] The critical override is **global** (evaluated before any tier loop): a critical in `plan_complete` outranks a non-critical `audit`, and a critical `idea` outranks a non-critical `implement`, matching the intent "jump to the front of the queue". The existing freeze (audit/implement skipped while frozen) and caps (`risk <= Medium && effort <= Medium` for `plan_complete`, including critical) are retained.
- [ ] After a successful dispatch (or a `spawn-failed`/`marker-write-failed` claim that still consumes the entry), the round-robin cursor/state advances to mark that project's `worklogRoot` as most-recently served, so the next dispatch in **any** tier starts from the following project.
- [ ] Existing `downtime-worker` and `coordination` tests still pass, plus new tests prove: (a) with two non-critical entries from different projects at the same tier, consecutive dispatches alternate projects; (b) a newly-arrived critical from project B is dispatched next even though round-robin would choose project A; (c) cursor persists across a simulated leader restart.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints
- Must build on the existing coordination machinery (`packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` lock + atomic write, `machine-coordination.ts` single machine dir) — no new daemon or external dependency.
- Fail-open on missing/corrupt round-robin state (behaves as if no history — original file order), never throws or starves dispatch.
- No behaviour change to `wl next` / single-project flows; this is strictly the multi-project leader path (`coordinationDir` present).
- Preserve dispatched-marker exclusion and CAS claim ordering already in `dispatchFromCoordination`.
- Each project currently registers at most one offer per cycle, so per-project multiplicity can be treated as one entry per root — design should not break if that grows, but need not optimise for many-per-root.

## Existing State
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchFromCoordination` groups fetched entries by tier (`audit` → `critical` → `implement` → `plan` → `intake`) and iterates each group in file order (`entries` array order). No cross-project fairness: repeated offers from the same root can win every slot when they re-queue quickly.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin.ts` provides a per-tier persistent cursor for the *legacy* `selectWithRotation` path (unused in coordination mode); the new requirement is **global, cross-tier** round-robin across `worklogRoot`s.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` manages `downtime-coordination.json` with atomic tmp+rename and an `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` lock (`tryAcquireCoordLock` / `withCoordLock`), and already carries `worklogRoot` per entry; `machine-coordination.ts` makes the file machine-wide.
- Tests: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/coordination.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/coordination-cross-root.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin.test.ts`.
- Contributing projects: ContextHub, SorraAgents, AI_Hell, Tableau-Card-Engine (each instance writes one entry via `runCoordinationCheckIn`).

## Desired Change
- Introduce a **global per-project round-robin** ordering for `dispatchFromCoordination`: track last-dispatched `worklogRoot` (persistent JSON alongside the coordination file, e.g. `downtime-round-robin-by-root.json`), sort same-tier eligible candidates by "least-recently-served first" before dispatch, and advance the cursor on each consumed entry.
- Promote the **critical override** to a global pre-tier check: re-fetch → if any dispatchable critical exists, dispatch the first critical immediately (respecting freeze/caps), before the tier-ordered round-robin loop.
- Add/extend tests to cover alternating-project fairness, critical jump-ahead, and cursor durability; update `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and relevant code comments.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Needs updated `dispatchFromCoordination` + new helpers for global round-robin ordering / cursor advance
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — May gain small helpers or remain unchanged (new state file is separate)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin.ts` — May be reused/extended or a new `downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts` added for worklogRoot-keyed persistence
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — Reference for machine-dir resolution used by the new state file
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — Needs new fair-scheduling test cases
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — Needs updated dispatch ordering description (fair scheduling + critical override)

## Related Work
- Parent area: `WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL` (Refactor Downtime Dispatcher: leader election + shared coordination file), `WL-0MTF0KLO10043YAN` (Single machine-wide leader), `WL-0MTII45EP002DWK6` (Cross-directory tier dispatch)
- Preceding round-robin work: `WL-0MSSRED76008LGB6` + `downtime-round-robin.ts` / `downtime-round-robin.test.ts` (per-tier cursor, now superseded by global root-level rotation)
- Tier / dispatch reference: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:COORDINATION_TIER_ORDER`, `classifyItemForDispatch`, `COORDINATION_FILE` / `readCoordinationFile` in `coordination.ts`
- Follow-up opportunity: if per-root multiplicity grows beyond one, consider weighted or deficit round-robin (record as a linked work item, not in scope)

## Risks & Assumptions
- **Risk:** Cursor file races between leaders → Mitigation: reuse the existing `withCoordLock` / tmp+rename pattern; fail-open when lock is contended.
- **Risk:** New critical items arriving between fetch and dispatch could be missed → Mitigation: critical check happens on the same single fetch pass; subsequent arrivals wait one cycle (acceptable at 30-min check-in cadence).
- **Risk:** Stale-entry pruning removes a root before its round-robin turn → Mitigation: pruned roots drop from ordering automatically; no ghost cursor entries block others.
- **Risk:** Scope creep (e.g. per-entry priority weighting beyond critical) → Mitigation: explicitly out of scope; non-critical priorities are treated as equally round-robined (per operator: one item per project).
- **Assumption:** At most one entry per `worklogRoot` per cycle — holds today; ordering by `worklogRoot` last-served is equivalent to ordering by entry last-served.
- **Assumption:** "Jump to the front" means dispatch before any non-critical regardless of tier, not just within the same tier — confirmed with operator (clarification round: globally, dispatch immediately).
- **Assumption:** Persistence should survive leader restarts and machine reboot → file on disk in the machine coordination dir, not in-memory only.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "What constitutes a 'project' for fair scheduling?" — Answer (user): "The multi-project downtime scheduling recently implemented — leader election with one work item per project via the herdr extension. Currently ContextHub, ../SorraAgents, ../AI_Hell, ../Tableau-Card-Engine." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "Is this about `wl next` or the coordination dispatch?" — Answer (user): "The multi-project case — nothing to do with `wl next`." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "When a project has a critical item, does it jump the queue?" — Answer (user): "yes" (affirmative — critical from any project jumps ahead). Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "Do non-critical priorities (high/medium/low) matter within round-robin?" — Answer (user): "I believe each project only registers a single work item so this is not important." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "Round-robin scope — per-tier or globally?" — Answer (user): "globally" Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "Critical override granularity — immediate dispatch or just cursor bump?" — Answer (user): "dispatch immediately" Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "Should the cursor persist across cycles/restarts?" — Answer (user): "persistent" Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
data.title: Fair round-robin work scheduling with priority override

**Goal:** Wire the global cursor into coordination dispatch for non-critical entries and advance it on consume.

## Implementation Summary
- Added imports: `loadRoundRobinCursor` and `advanceRoot` from `downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts`
- Added `sortEntriesByRoundRobin(group, coordinationDir)` helper: pure stable sort using cursor data (unknown roots first, oldest known first, file-order ties preserved), fail-open on missing/corrupt cursor

- Non-critical tier dispatched/spawn-failed/marker-write-failed: calls `removeEntry` + `advanceRoundRobinCursor`

- Cursor module (downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts) not modified — consumed as dependency
- Pure sort decoupled from cursor advance — cursor only advances on consumed entries
