# Log the dispatcher's actual no-dispatch reason (make gate decisions observable)

Parent RCA: WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28.

## Goal

Make it possible to diagnose "idle slots but no dispatches" from the logs alone. This RCA took hours
because the gate decision was invisible: the only persisted outcomes are successful dispatches and
3-strike errors.

## Problem

`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `tick()` returns neutral outcomes for several blockers
without recording *why*:

- `slotOwned` → `{ polled: true, dispatched: false, idle: true }` (no log)
- `contentionQueueDepth > 0` → same (no log)
- `no-candidate` / `review-queue-hold` / `code-freeze` / `fresh-audit-skip` / `audit-in-flight`
- the idle-duration gate not yet met (`polled: true, idle: true`)

The herdr header only distinguishes dispatching / off / paused / idle / busy, and idle only shows
when *all* slots are idle (per-slot tracker). There is no record of `slotOwned` blocking dispatch,
so the proxy UI shows idle slots while the dispatcher is refusing.

## Required behaviour

- On each tick that polls and does not dispatch, append a structured entry to
  `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` (or a dedicated decision log) with: outcome reason, free
  slot count / total slots, owner present, `runningPanes`, contention depth, and tick timestamp.
- Rate-limit / de-duplicate so a healthy idle loop does not flood the log (e.g. log on reason
  change or at most once per N minutes per instance).
- Surface the current blocking reason in the worklist header (extend `renderDowntimeStatus`, e.g.
  `[downtime held: slot-owner]`) without changing the existing state labels.
- Do not log on every 10s tick while genuinely idle-and-eligible (no candidate vs gate-blocked are
  distinct): only record actionable refusals.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A tick refused by `slotOwned` writes one decision log line containing the reason and the
   observed slot/owner fields.
2. A tick refused by `contentionQueueDepth > 0` writes the reason and depth.
3. Repeated identical refusals are rate-limited (bounded lines per hour) — asserted by test.
4. The header shows the active blocking reason distinct from plain `idle`/`busy`.
5. Existing dispatch/error log schemas are unchanged (additive only); all consumers/tests updated.
data.title: Downtime dispatcher: log the actual no-dispatch reason (slotOwned/contention/no-candidate) + header

# Re-verify the local dispatch-lease TTL assumption; exclude leases held by our own panes

Parent RCA: WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28.

## Goal

Align the dispatcher's owner-lease model with what the proxy actually does, so the gate is neither
over- nor under-conservative.

## Problem

`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` documents and relies on the assumption that local proxy
leases "expire ~180 s after activity stops". Observation from the live proxy contradicts this:
during UTC 00:01–00:12 a dispatched pane's lease was `local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds`
**836 → 0** (≈840 s), i.e. an order of magnitude longer than the code assumes. The proxy
(`llm-manager` `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`) computes an **adaptive** lease with
`local_dispatch_lease_max_seconds` defaulting to 1500 s, plus chunk/prefill refresh buffers. So a
long agent generation holds the lease for its whole run.

Consequence: any gate keyed on "lease held" blocks for the entire generation, not ~3 minutes.
This amplifies the `slotOwned` defect (the per-slot fix is the primary remedy; this item removes the
stale assumption and the self-blocking case).

## Required behaviour

- Re-read the proxy lease semantics (static + adaptive + refresh buffers) and document the real
  bounds in `downtime-worker.ts`, replacing the "~180 s" claim.
- If the dispatcher spawns a pane, it knows that pane's session id; a lease held by one of the
  dispatcher's own live panes must not be treated as "someone else owns the target slot"
  (it already owns its slot, not the free ones).
- Keep fail-closed behaviour when the proxy serves no lease information.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The lease-TTL comment/constant in `downtime-worker.ts` reflects the proxy's actual maximum
   (adaptive lease max), with a unit test bounding the waited-out/refusal behaviour.
2. A lease attributable to a dispatcher-spawned pane does not block dispatch into other unowned
   free slots (test).
3. No regression: a lease held by an unknown/operator session on a count-based single-slot setup
   still blocks dispatch.
4. `docs/` (or the module header) records the proxy lease contract and the cross-repo dependency
   (`llm-manager`), so the assumption does not silently drift again.

## Notes

- Cross-repo: the lease implementation lives in `llm-manager` (`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`).
  If that repo changes the defaults, this item's constant must be revisited.
data.title: Downtime dispatcher: correct local dispatch-lease TTL assumption; do not block on leases held by own panes

# Intake Brief: Client retry does not honor Retry-After (503 startup_ramp)

## Problem statement

The llm-proxy's **post-restart startup ramp** gate returns HTTP `503` with a
randomized `Retry-After` header (5-18 s) and a machine-readable body
(`{"error":{"type":"startup_ramp","code":"startup_ramp","message":"Server is starting up; retry shortly."},"status":503,"retry_after":N}`)
specifically so that clients spread their reconnects across the ramp window
(`startup_ramp.max_seconds: 180` in `proxy/config.yaml`; proxy side tracked as
LP-0MUA6RAMP001XXXX).

The Pi client does **not** honor that hint. Its *agent-level* auto-retry
(`getRetrySettings()` -> `retryDelayMs() = baseDelayMs * 2 ** (attempt - 1)`,
`baseDelayMs` default 2000 ms, cap 60 000 ms, **no jitter**) ignores both the
`Retry-After` header and the `retry_after` body field.

### Evidence (2026-09-20)

Proxy restarted at 16:11:28 local; the 180 s startup ramp was active until
~16:14:28. Session `herdr-1789917126-2590234-11663` (model `plan`, provider
`Local Proxy`), every turn failing with
`503: {"type":"startup_ramp",...}`:

| attempt | time (local) | gap vs prev |
|---------|--------------|-------------|
| 1       | 16:12:10.5   | -           |
| 2       | 16:12:12.6   | +2.0 s      |
| 3       | 16:12:16.6   | +4.0 s      |
| 4       | 16:12:24.6   | +8.0 s      |
| 5       | 16:12:40.7   | +16.0 s     |
| 6       | 16:13:12.8   | +32.1 s     |
| 7       | 16:14:13.1   | +60.3 s     |

This is exactly `2000 * 2^(attempt-1)` capped at 60 000 ms - the client's own
deterministic backoff, independent of the `Retry-After` values the proxy
returned (random randint in [5,15] + 3 s margin per request, logged by the
proxy as `Startup ramp: deferring chat request (... retry_after=Ns)`).

A second session (`herdr-1789917234-2590706-9592`, this very analysis session)
shows the same `+2.0 / +4.0 / +8.0` pattern.

## Impact

1. Clients retry **sooner than instructed** (e.g. `Retry-After: 7` -> retry at
   2 s), hammering the freshly restarted proxy - the opposite of the ramp's
   intent.
2. Backoff has **no jitter**, so clients that started together retry in
   lockstep, defeating the ramp's desynchronisation goal.
3. The retry cap (`maxAgentDelayMs` 60 s) is shorter than the ramp window (up
   to 180 s), so a client can exhaust its retry budget mid-ramp and surface a
   hard failure to the user even though the server said "retry shortly".

## Users

- Operators/developers running herdr workers (Pi agents) against the local
  llm-proxy.
- Anyone whose first provider request after a mode switch / proxy restart lands
  inside the ramp window.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1**: When an OpenAI-compatible provider response carries `Retry-After`
  (delta-seconds or HTTP-date) and the request is retried, the client's delay is
  at least the server-requested delay (bounded by a configurable maximum,
  default 60 s).
- **AC2**: The `503 startup_ramp` body's `retry_after` field is honored as a
  fallback when the header is absent or unparseable.
- **AC3**: Missing/malformed hints fall back to the existing exponential
  backoff, unchanged.
- **AC4**: A client can survive a full startup ramp (up to
  `startup_ramp.max_seconds`, default 180 s) without exhausting its retry budget,
  or the ramp window is otherwise communicated so a long ramp does not surface
  as a final user-visible failure solely because the retry budget ran out first.
- **AC5**: Jitter is applied to (or combined with) any delay derived from the
  server hint so concurrent clients do not retry in lockstep.
- **AC6**: Tests cover header/body parsing, the cap, malformed values, and the
  long-ramp case; full suite green.
- **AC7**: No double-retry amplification between the provider-level and
  agent-level retry layers.

## Constraints

- Tracked in ContextHub; the change belongs in the **Pi coding agent codebase**
  (same arrangement as WL-0MPWVLT6Q0064MUO).
- Pi already exposes a provider-level helper that *does* honor
  `retry-after`/`retry-after-ms` (`@earendil-works/pi-ai` -> `retryProviderRequest`),
  but it is effectively disabled: `openai-completions` calls it with
  `maxRetries` from `settings.retry.provider.maxRetries`, which is unset
  (-> 0). The active layer is the agent-level retry in `settings-manager` /
  `agent-session` / `retry.ts`, which ignores the hint. Reuse/extend the
  existing helper rather than adding a third retry path.
- Keep the change minimal; do not regress the completed
  WL-0MPWVLT6Q0064MUO tuning. Note: the installed build observed here still
  shows `baseDelayMs = 2000` (not 7000), so verify version drift before
  assuming that tuning is present.

## Related work

- WL-0MPWVLT6Q0064MUO (completed) - "When a model is loading wait longer before
  retrying" (increased agent retry delays; did **not** add Retry-After honoring).
- llm-proxy startup ramp: LP-0MUA6RAMP001XXXX (proxy side, `/home/rgardler/projects/llm`).
- llm-proxy `Retry-After` emission: LP-0MPQ2PLTC000GYRZ, LP-0MQS6MPK9000UIZK.

## Out of scope

- The proxy-side startup-ramp behaviour itself (tracked in the llm project).

# Ship report to Discord needs titling

## Problem statement

The Discord ship report embed title is hardcoded as `Release vX.Y.Z` and does not include the project name from the worklog config. Additionally, the report description should include the project name for clarity.

## Users

- **Release operator**: Wants the Discord notification to clearly identify which project is being released, especially when monitoring multiple project releases.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The Discord embed title changes from `Release vX.Y.Z` to `<ProjectName> Release vX.Y.Z`, where `<ProjectName>` is read from the worklog config's `projectName` field.
2. The project name is resolved from `<project>/.worklog/config.yaml` (same config path used for webhook URL resolution), with fallback to the global config `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml`.
3. If the config is missing or `projectName` is absent, the title gracefully falls back to `Release vX.Y.Z`.
4. The embed description includes the project name alongside the version for added clarity.
5. All existing unit tests pass, with updated assertions reflecting the new title format.

## Constraints

- Non-breaking change — existing webhook behaviour must not be affected.
- The YAML parser (`parseSimpleYaml`) already handles top-level `projectName` keys.
- Must use the same config resolution precedence as the webhook URL (project config first, then global).

## Existing state

- `buildDiscordPayload()` in `discord-notify.js` hardcodes the title: `title: Release v${versionText}`.
- The `parseSimpleYaml()` function already parses `projectName` from config (verified in tests).
- `resolveDiscordWebhookUrl()` already follows the correct precedence pattern.
- The `sendReleaseNotification()` function resolves the webhook URL but does not read `projectName`.

## Desired change

1. Add a `resolveProjectName(projectRoot)` helper (parallel to `resolveDiscordWebhookUrl`) that reads `projectName` from the worklog config.
2. Update `sendReleaseNotification()` to resolve the project name and pass it to `buildDiscordPayload()`.
3. Update `buildDiscordPayload()` to accept a `projectName` parameter and include it in the embed title and description.

## Key Files

- `scripts/discord-notify.js` — Add project name resolution and update payload builder
- `tests/test_discord_notify.mjs` — Update title assertions from `Release v1.2.3` to `<ProjectName> Release v1.2.3`

## Related work

- `WL-0MUB023JP001A9N3` — This work item itself (ship skill Discord notification)

## Note on bot name

The "bot name" that appears in Discord messages is controlled by the webhook URL configuration within Discord's channel settings, not by application code. This cannot be fixed programmatically — it requires configuring the webhook's display name in Discord. The fix addresses what CAN be controlled: the embed title and description content.

# Goal

As a herdr operator, I want the downtime dispatcher to open at most one pane per
work item per skill while a prior dispatch is still in-flight, so concurrent
agents never share a worktree/branch or fight over the same files.

# Headline finding

On 2026-09-21 the downtime dispatcher spawned `/skill:implement` **twice** for
the same **critical** item within hours, producing two concurrent pi agents on
the **same** worktree and branch:

| Root | Kind | Item | Count | First dispatch | Last dispatch | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| /home/rgardler/projects/llm | implement | LP-0MUAY98ZR002JBAA | 2 | 2026-09-21T11:04:55.378Z | 2026-09-21T11:30:31.129Z | 25m36s |
| /home/rgardler/projects/llm | implement | LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO | 2 | 2026-09-21T11:33:49.028Z | 2026-09-21T13:54:33.548Z | 2h20m45s |

Both items are `priority: critical` (startup-ramp work). This is a recurrence of
`WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT` (which covered the audit/plan tiers) in the **implement**
tier, and it is **not** the same-instant TOCTOU race (that RCA's RC-1) — the gaps
are minutes-to-hours.

# Impact (observed damage)

- Two pi sessions ran the same instruction concurrently in the SAME worktree
  (`wl-LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO-startup-ramp-only-gate-chat-requests-tha`):
  - `herdr-1789990429-2794297-1569` (first dispatch, 11:33:49Z)
  - `herdr-1789998873-2814350-14820` (duplicate, 13:54:33Z)
- A concurrent `git pull origin dev` in the shared worktree merged the
  newly-landed sibling commit (`LP-0MUAY98ZR002JBAA`, `4080d2f1`) into
  uncommitted local work and left `UU` (unmerged) index entries and conflict
  markers in `proxy/proxy/ui.py` and `proxy/tests/test_startup_ramp.py`.
- The two agents thrashed the same files: one agent ran `git reset --hard HEAD`
  (discarding the other's working-tree edits) and both eventually
  committed/pushed the same commit (`0df744ec`); both posted
  "Implementation complete" comments for the same commit.
- Wasted compute: ~2h20m 45s of duplicated agent time, duplicate full-suite
  runs, duplicate audit, and a near-miss duplicate commit.

# Evidence

## 1. Dispatcher log — `/home/rgardler/projects/llm/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`

Verbatim entries for the two affected items (the dispatcher writes one JSONL
line per spawned pane; this file is capped at the most recent
`DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES` = 100 entries):

```json
{"itemId":"LP-0MUAY98ZR002JBAA","kind":"implement","dispatchedAt":"2026-09-21T11:04:55.378Z","cwd":"/home/rgardler/projects/llm","title":"Startup ramp: shorten the window and clear the gate when backends are ready","stage":"plan_complete"}
{"itemId":"LP-0MUAY98ZR002JBAA","kind":"implement","dispatchedAt":"2026-09-21T11:30:31.129Z","cwd":"/home/rgardler/projects/llm","title":"Startup ramp: shorten the window and clear the gate when backends are ready","stage":"plan_complete"}
{"itemId":"LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO","kind":"implement","dispatchedAt":"2026-09-21T11:33:49.028Z","cwd":"/home/rgardler/projects/llm","title":"Startup ramp: only gate chat requests that would dispatch locally","stage":"plan_complete"}
{"itemId":"LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO","kind":"implement","dispatchedAt":"2026-09-21T13:54:33.548Z","cwd":"/home/rgardler/projects/llm","title":"Startup ramp: only gate chat requests that would dispatch locally","stage":"plan_complete"}
```

Notes:
- Neither implement entry carries `outcome: "spawn-failed"`, so
  `dispatchedItemMarkers` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts:273`) treats both
  as SUCCESS markers that should suppress re-selection.
- Both entries recorded `stage: "plan_complete"`, i.e. the item's stage did
  **not** advance between dispatches.

## 2. Duplicate scan (canonical tool)

```
$ python3 packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py /home/rgardler/projects/llm --since 2026-09-20T00:00:00Z --json
count: 2
implement LP-0MUAY98ZR002JBAA x2 2026-09-21T11:04:55.378Z -> 2026-09-21T11:30:31.129Z gap=1536s
implement LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO x2 2026-09-21T11:33:49.028Z -> 2026-09-21T13:54:33.548Z gap=8445s
```

(Note: `/home/rgardler/projects/llm` is **not** in the scanner's
`DEFAULT_ROOTS`, so this root must be passed explicitly.)

## 3. Work-item comment timeline (`LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO`)

```
2026-09-21T09:43:08.412Z | herdr-downtime | Auto-dispatched ... running /skill:intake LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO.
2026-09-21T10:54:05.185Z | herdr-downtime | Auto-dispatched ... running /skill:plan LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO.
2026-09-21T11:33:49.109Z | herdr-downtime | Auto-dispatched ... running /skill:implement LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO.   <-- dispatch #1
2026-09-21T11:34:55.549Z | implement      | Start phase: 13 orphaned stash(es) detected ...
2026-09-21T11:35:04.154Z | implement      | Implementation started - Worktree: .../wl-LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO-... - Branch: wl-...
2026-09-21T13:54:33.633Z | herdr-downtime | Auto-dispatched ... running /skill:implement LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO.   <-- dispatch #2 (duplicate)
2026-09-21T14:48:12.031Z | herdr-downtime | Implementation complete: - Commit: 0df744ec ...
2026-09-21T14:48:22.006Z | Map            | Implementation complete and pushed to dev (commit 0df744ec). ...
```

Critically, at 11:34:55Z the first dispatch had claimed the item
(`status: in_progress`; the run also logged `WARNING: Failed to update stage`,
so the stage stayed `plan_complete`). A direct `wl show` at 14:26Z still reported
`status: in_progress | stage: plan_complete`, bracketing the 13:54:33Z
re-dispatch.

## 4. Coordination log — `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`

The worker checked in on the item roughly every 4 minutes from 09:42:06Z to
13:52:06Z (single instance `c8132593-6b06-46f5-b24f-f2eee545cdb9`), then
re-dispatched at 13:54:33Z. First 4 and last 4 check-ins:

```json
{"kind":"coordination","operation":"checkin","instanceId":"c8132593-6b06-46f5-b24f-f2eee545cdb9","workItemId":"LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO","at":"2026-09-21T09:42:06.877Z"}
{"kind":"coordination","operation":"checkin","instanceId":"c8132593-6b06-46f5-b24f-f2eee545cdb9","workItemId":"LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO","at":"2026-09-21T10:50:37.575Z"}
{"kind":"coordination","operation":"checkin","instanceId":"c8132593-6b06-46f5-b24f-f2eee545cdb9","workItemId":"LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO","at":"2026-09-21T11:05:03.204Z"}
{"kind":"coordination","operation":"checkin","instanceId":"c8132593-6b06-46f5-b24f-f2eee545cdb9","workItemId":"LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO","at":"2026-09-21T11:30:45.348Z"}
...
{"kind":"coordination","operation":"checkin","instanceId":"c8132593-6b06-46f5-b24f-f2eee545cdb9","workItemId":"LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO","at":"2026-09-21T13:39:48.185Z"}
{"kind":"coordination","operation":"checkin","instanceId":"c8132593-6b06-46f5-b24f-f2eee545cdb9","workItemId":"LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO","at":"2026-09-21T13:43:49.326Z"}
{"kind":"coordination","operation":"checkin","instanceId":"c8132593-6b06-46f5-b24f-f2eee545cdb9","workItemId":"LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO","at":"2026-09-21T13:47:59.540Z"}
{"kind":"coordination","operation":"checkin","instanceId":"c8132593-6b06-46f5-b24f-f2eee545cdb9","workItemId":"LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO","at":"2026-09-21T13:52:06.754Z"}
```

The item remained the worker's top candidate across the whole window — it was
tracked every cycle and then re-dispatched rather than skipped.

## 5. Concurrent sessions

- Session 1 (first dispatch): `herdr-1789990429-2794297-1569`, start
  2026-09-21T11:33:49Z, PID 2794306. Session file:
  `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-llm--/2026-09-21T11-33-49-321Z_herdr-1789990429-2794297-1569.jsonl`
- Session 2 (duplicate): `herdr-1789998873-2814350-14820`, start
  2026-09-21T13:54:33Z, PID 2814359. Session file:
  `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-llm--/2026-09-21T13-54-33-846Z_herdr-1789998873-2814350-14820.jsonl`

Both sessions were alive simultaneously for >1h (session 2's last write
15:50Z; session 1 still running at report time).

# Code analysis (pointers)

Both selection paths appear to require the item's CURRENT status to be `open`:

- Normal Herdr-head scan: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:2455` —
  `if (status !== 'open') return null;` in `classifyItemForDispatch`.
- Critical-first scan: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:1895` —
  `.filter((i) => i.priority === 'critical' && i.status === 'open' && i.needsProducerReview !== true)`.
- Coordination path: `dispatchFromCoordination` re-fetches the item and runs
  `classifyItemForDispatch` (same status gate) — see the dispatch-site comment
  at `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:2710-2745` ("a stale offer — item
  closed/in_progress/review-gated ... is dropped").

Dispatched-marker exclusion:

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts:273` `dispatchedItemMarkers` (skips only
  `outcome === 'spawn-failed'`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts:310` `markerStillExcludes` — a marker
  excludes only while `marker.stage === itemStage` AND age ≤ the staleness
  window.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:266-284` — staleness window default
  24h, hard floor 1h, ceiling 7d.

Critical-first scan **bypasses** the marker exclusion:

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:1935-1966` — the loop's own comment:
  "this loop bypasses the non-safety filters (dispatched-marker exclusion,
  review-queue depth hold)". It dispatches critical candidates directly through
  `dispatchClaimedTier` (CAS claim only).
- The normal head scan consults `markerMaps[k]` before dispatching
  (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:1994-2006`).

Rolling log is rewritten non-atomically:

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts:75-76` `DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES = 100`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts:411-431` `appendRollingJsonl` reads the
  whole file, appends, trims, then `writeFile` rewrites it. A concurrent
  `readDowntimeLogEntries` (fail-safe → `[]`) can observe an empty/partial file
  and thus an empty marker set.

Stage did not advance:

- The first implement run logged `WARNING: Failed to update stage`; the stage
  stayed `plan_complete` (status `in_progress`). Had the stage advanced to
  `in_progress`, `markerStillExcludes` would have released the marker on the
  stage change — i.e. the marker was already the *only* remaining guard.

# Hypotheses (ranked)

- **H1 (primary) — critical-first scan bypasses the marker exclusion.** Critical
  items are intentionally re-dispatched despite a fresh success marker
  (`downtime-worker.ts:1935`). Both duplicated items are `priority: critical`.
  The only serialisation on that loop is the `dispatchClaimedTier` CAS claim,
  which prevents same-instant races but not a later idle cycle. Caveat: the loop
  filters `status === 'open'`, so this requires the dispatcher's item snapshot to
  still show `open` (see H2).
- **H2 — stale item status in the dispatcher's snapshot.** Selection operates on
  the `items` supplied by the Herdr list; if that snapshot was not refreshed
  after the first agent's `in_progress` claim, the critical item stays a
  candidate and H1's bypass fires.
- **H3 — non-atomic rolling-log rewrite defeats the marker set.** A marker read
  concurrent with `appendRollingJsonl`'s full-file rewrite can see `[]`
  (fail-safe), making an item look never-dispatched. This explains a re-dispatch
  without any stage change on a marker-guarded path.
- **H4 — multiple leaders/instances.** Only one `instanceId` appears in the
  coordination log, but if two workers briefly overlapped, their CAS claims and
  marker reads are coordinated only through the shared, non-atomically rewritten
  file — compounding H1/H3.
- **H5 — marker-write failure/rollback for the first dispatch.** Would leave the
  item re-eligible; both log entries lack `outcome`, so the first entry's marker

  vs H4) with a reproduction or targeted instrumentation.
- **AC2**: A `priority: critical` item is never dispatched twice for the same
  skill while a prior dispatch is in-flight (live pane and/or an unexpired
  claim), regardless of marker freshness or stage.
- **AC3**: Preserve the critical-first escalation intent (a critical item
  blocked by a stale marker must still progress) without re-dispatching an
  in-flight item — e.g. bound escalation to once per claim TTL, or gate on a
  live-pane / in-flight check.
- **AC4**: Make the rolling dispatch/coordination log read-modify-write atomic
  (write temp + `rename`) so a concurrent marker read can never observe an
  empty/partial log.
- **AC5**: Regression test: two idle cycles with a critical implement item still
  at the same stage and already claimed/in-flight → exactly one dispatch (both
  the Herdr-head and coordination paths).
- **AC6**: Dispatcher log entries record the session/pane id and the selection
  path/reason for each dispatch — currently only
  `itemId/kind/dispatchedAt/cwd/title/stage`, which made this RCA's
  path attribution manual.

  recurrence for critical items.

  lifecycle.

# Out of scope

- Other pre-existing duplicate pairs from before 2026-09-21 (visible in the full
  scan).
- The correctness of the code delivered by `LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO` (already merged
  to `dev` as `0df744ec`).

# Assumptions

- `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` is the authoritative record of dispatches
  (one entry per spawned pane), and no manual/operator dispatch occurred at
  13:54:33Z — the `herdr-downtime` comment timestamp matches the log entry.

Root cause identified and fixed:
  
The header truncation (commit 92841448) and emoji fix (commit 71374acb) were correct but incomplete.

and always counted visLen += 1 (never handled multi-width). When work items had CJK titles

1. Expanded visibleLength() to handle 15 double-width Unicode ranges (CJK, Hangul, fullwidth, etc.)
2. Updated formatItemLine() to use visibleLength() and multi-width-aware truncation loop
3. Updated formatTooltipOverlay() to use visibleLength()
4. Updated dialog padLine() to use visibleLength()
5. Added 3 new tests: CJK title truncation, CJK rows-1 invariant, fullwidth ASCII

All 365 tests pass.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
question: OpenBrain error — root cause found; scope of "Remove openbrain" needs producer confirmation before intake can finish.

## Root cause of the OpenBrain error

- This project's `.worklog/config.yaml` sets `openBrainEnabled: true` (added by commit `66fb51a8` "Enable OpenBrain for local testing"). No sibling project enables it, which is why the error is seen here only.
- When enabled, `wl update` (status → `completed`) and `wl close` call `submitToOpenBrain()` in `src/openbrain.ts`, which spawns the `ob` (OpenBrain) CLI via `child_process.spawn`.
- The `ob` binary is **not installed** on PATH (and `WL_OB_BIN` is unset), so the spawn fails and writes `[openbrain] …` errors to stderr. The call is fire-and-forget, so the work-item write still succeeds — only the error output is visible.

## Blocking question — what does "Remove openbrain" mean?

- **(A) Remove the feature from the shared `worklog` codebase**: delete `src/openbrain.ts`, the `openBrainEnabled` config field (`packages/shared/src/types.ts`), the call sites in `src/commands/update.ts` / `src/commands/close.ts`, the tests (`tests/unit/openbrain.test.ts`, `tests/cli/openbrain-close.test.ts`) and `docs/openbrain.md`. ~600 lines; affects every project that uses `wl`.
- **(B) Only stop the error in this project**: remove/disable the `openBrainEnabled: true` line in `.worklog/config.yaml` (one line), leaving the optional feature available to other projects.

The work-item **title** ("Remove openbrain") points at (A); the **description** ("In this project, but not any other … find where this is coming from and disable it") points at (B). Because (A) and (B) differ by roughly three orders of magnitude in blast radius across a shared CLI, intake is paused until the scope is confirmed.

Reply with `A`, `B`, or `both`.

# Investigation: downtime dispatcher vs herdr selection list — divergence brief

## Summary (investigation only — no code changes)

Herdr's selection list and the downtime dispatcher disagree because they
start from **different input sets, staged through different pipelines,**
and grouped into different presentational shapes. `wl next`'s
`packages/shared/src/database.ts:computeScore`/`reSort` ranking
(AC3 determination, WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS) is the canonical "most
important" — the herdr list and the dispatcher both need to be aligned
to it (scope of WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2).

## Exact code paths compared

- Herdr list (what the producer browses with `prefix+l`):
  - `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems(count)`:
    - `wl next -n N --include-in-progress` (auto `reSort` of the full score
      order via `getAllOrderedByScore(recencyPolicy)` + `assignSortIndexValues`)
      — `wl next` without `-n` returns the *single* top candidate;
      with `-n` it returns the score-ordered batch up to the hard cap
      (default 32, hard-capped on the CLI side regardless of `browseItemCount`).
    - Also fetches `fetchMandatorySubsets()`:
      - `wl list --priority critical --root-only`
      - `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only`
      run in parallel and merged by ID (first wins).
    - Merged set fed through `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems(merged, browseItemCount)`
      — mandatory (critical ∪ completed/in_review, root-only, not `done`)
      always shown; `browseItemCount` caps ONLY the remaining "other"
      items, then `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems`
      re-groups every displayed item.
  - `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` filters to
    `!parentId && stage !== done`, mandatory-always logic,
    "others" limited to `browseItemCount - mandatory.length`.
  - `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` calls
    `assignItemGroups` → `groupItemsByFilePaths` partitioning;
    rendered with collapsible group headings via `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.

- Downtime dispatcher (what runs when slots are idle):
  - `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork`
    dispatched tiers in fixed order: **audit** →
    **critical**(`getNextCriticalCandidate` / `computeMostImportantItem`) →
    **implement**(`getNextImplementCandidate`) →
    **plan**(`wl next --stage intake_complete`) →
    **intake**(`wl next --stage idea`), each with its own
    input source and post-filtering.
  - Legacy "scheduled-prompts" stage runs *before* any tier if a
    due prompt exists (`getDueScheduledPrompt`).
  - Shared ranking is `packages/shared/src/database.ts`:
    `filterCandidates` → `handleCriticalEscalation` →
    `findNextWorkItemFromItems` / `getNextWorkItem` →
    `getAllOrderedByScore` → `computeScore` → `reSort` →
    `selectBySortIndex` ordering (falling back to
    audit-not-ready boost + effective-priority + age when sortIndex equal).

## Live sample (2026-09-02, ContextHub root, `browseItemCount=20`)

Current database snapshot (`wl next -n 20 --include-in-progress`):
- 20-item result (top by `wl next -n 20` score, with grouping metadata):
  1. WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q critical plan_complete in_progress (Critical Group 1)
  2. WL-0MTIB7JAN004MQ8N critical in_progress in_progress (Critical Group 2)
  3. WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V high plan_complete in_progress
  4. WL-0MSNI6TQ5003JY1Z high intake_complete open
  5. WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9 high plan_complete open
  6–8. other intake_complete open
  9–16. high idea (open + in_progress) + medium idea
  17–20. medium/in_progress idea + in_review candidates
  - mandatory sets merged: 2 critical root (non-done) + 1 completed/in_review root
  - all mandatory items already fell within the top-20 wl-next window at this
    snapshot so herdr's merged view and the raw `wl next -n 20` window
    agreed; at larger backlogs they diverge (cap 32 above).

Downtime dispatcher on same snapshot:
- Audit tier: 1 candidate (WL-0MTCP0ILG008YV84 completed/in_review)
- Implement tier: WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9 (open plan_complete, risk Medium ≤ Medium, effort Medium ≤ Medium)
- Plan/intake tiers: 0 open intake_complete; 0 open idea (all blocked by dep or status)
- Critical tier: 0 critical open root (none available)
- Result: dispatcher selects **WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9** (implement tier) as most-important,
  which appears in the herdr top-20 at position 5 today — agreement on this
  sample once filters are considered, but off-window candidates could land
  at rank 33+ of `wl next -n` while the herdr mandatory merge rescues them.

## Divergence gap map

| Dimension | Herdr list (`fetchNextItems`) | Downtime dispatcher (`dispatchDowntimeWork` / `computeMostImportantItem`) | Why they diverge |
|-----------|----------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------|
| **Input set / cap** | `wl next -n N` batch capped at 32; mandatory `wl list` merge bypasses the cap for critical+in_review | Stage-scoped `wl next --stage X` per tier (audit tier uses `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only` directly) + `wl list` for audit | A high-scored item beyond rank 32 in the wl-next global order is invisible to herdr unless it is critical/in_review; the dispatcher never calls `wl next -n N --include-in-progress` and so never sees that global window at all |
| **Stage filter** | No stage filter — global ranking across all stages | Per-tier call forces stage (`--stage plan_complete`/`intake_complete`/`idea`; audit forces `completed/in_review`) | Dispatcher scopes candidates by stage before ranking; herdr shows global top by score |
| **Risk/effort filter** | None in herdr list (risk/effort not applied server-side to the global `wl next -n` call) | Implement tier applies `risk ≤ Medium, effort ≤ Medium` (server-side filters; items with unset/empty risk/effort excluded, AC2) | A high plan_complete item with High/Severe risk or Large effort can appear in herdr top-20 but be invisible in the implement tier |
| **Audit tier, marker, recency** | No audit recency; no dispatched-marker exclusion; no "no valid audit in 7d" gate; in_review items grouped last via `assignItemGroups` | Audit tier: `wl list` caps 7-day recency window, no-valid-audit check, durable `dispatched-marker` exclusion, active-audit single-flight, 2h stale window, code-freeze tri-state gate (`frozen`/`ambiguous` skips audit+implement) | Same in_review item can appear at group 8 in herdr but at the TOP of the dispatcher when its updatedAt is recent |
| **Blocked / in_review handling** | Shows `in_review` in-review group last; `done` excluded; `blocked` filtered only by deltas | Per-tier `--\-status open` guard (plan/intake) excludes completed; dep-blocked items excluded via `filterCandidates` unless overridden; `includeInProgress` toggles with claim; ``other`` vs "dispatchable" exclusion | A blocked or completed/in_review item can be visible in herdr (mandatory/In Review) but never dispatchable; opposite unlikely (dispatcher cannot surface a child independently — see below) |
| **sortIndex / reSort / recency-policy** | `wl next` auto calls `reSort(recencyPolicy)` (default `ignore`); herdr's `regroupWorkItems` sorts by group number then `compareGroupableItems` (critical→plan/intake→idea→other→in_review, then stage order then priority then id) — NOT by sortIndex | Legacy dispatcher path's per-tier `wl next --stage` also triggers auto-`reSort`; coordination leader recomputes via `computeMostImportantItem` after fresh `wl show` + `isAuditFresh`; `sortIndex` used as tie-break only in leader's `--no-re-sort` path | Herdr grouping changes presentation order even within a score band — herdr position ≠ canonical `wl next` rank; `--recency-policy=prefer/avoid` could further shift wl-next batch while herdr's group sort is recency-agnostic |
| **Grouping vs flat ordering** | `regroupWorkItems` assigns file-path partitioning (critical vs Group N) and collapsible headings (WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94) | Dispatcher selects a *flat* single candidate (no group) — ranking comparison ignores file-path grouping | Divergence in "which work can safely he

## Reproducible sampling scripts

```bash
# wl next global score order (canonical; auto reSort with --recency-policy ignore)
wl next -n 20 --include-in-progress --json              # herdr fetcher base
wl next -n 500 --include-in-progress --json              # full 96-item order today

# Herdr mandatory subsets (merged by fetcher.ts)
wl list --priority critical --root-only --json
wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only --json

# Dispatcher per-tier selections (same snapshot)
wl next --stage plan_complete --json                     # implement tier base
wl next --stage plan_complete --risk Medium --effort Medium --json   # risk/effort caps
wl list --priority critical --status open --root-only --json         # critical tier
wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only --json      # audit tier

# Dispatcher audit logs + code-freeze marker
cat .worklog/downtime-dispatches.log | tail -20
cat .worklog/code-freeze.json   # tri-state gate: not-frozen / frozen / ambiguous

# Code-freeze / recency knobs
#   wl commands run reSort with --recency-policy (default ignore);
#   herdr grouping is recency-agnostic — record the flag used in samples.
```

`sortIndex` freshness: `wl next` CLI auto-calls `reSort(recencyPolicy)`; a stale
`sortIndex` (older `.worklog/worklog.db` row before the next CLI call) can make
two successive `-n` batches see different indexes — always record whether
`--no-re-sort` was used.

Ranking contract will be carried in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (+ herdr
README / `src/commands/next.ts --help` help text) under WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2.

leaves the existing `src/commands/next.ts` help and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
as-is — follow-up owns the unified contract wording.

## Risk / assumption note

- Coordination split: per-worklog `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` vs
  machine-wide coordination lease (leader-election) — "most important globally"
  vs per-worklog can still differ until unified behind wl next global score.
- Single-slot budgets (AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS=2 vs PANE_MIN_FREE_SLOTS=1) are not

- No code / test changes in this work item — evidence and gaps are sampled above.

data.comment:
# Audit Report: WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2 - FAILED

## Title
Dispatcher consumes Herdr selection list head (supersedes wl next unification)

## Status
**FAILED — Incomplete Implementation**

## Acceptance Criteria Assessment

### AC1: Dispatcher consumes Herdr list head — ❌ FAILED
**Expected:** `dispatchDowntimeWork` derives its candidate from the Herdr selection list head (`fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` → `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` → `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems`). No second ranking implementation.

**Actual:** `packages/herdr/src/index.ts:628` still contains the production no-op stub:
```typescript
getHerdrListHead: async (_cwd: string): Promise<...> => ({ ok: true, items: [] }),
```

The stub returns an empty items array. While `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:2149` does call `deps.getHerdrListHead(opts.cwd)`, the result is always empty, causing the dispatcher to fall through to the legacy tier chain.

**Evidence:**
- `index.ts` (current HEAD, same in commit 5594bbb2): line 628 returns `items: []`
- `downtime-worker.ts` line 2149-2150: `const head = await deps.getHerdrListHead(opts.cwd)` → always empty
- When `head.items.length === 0`, execution falls through to the legacy tier chain (lines 2168+)

### AC2: No duplicate ranking; gates are filters — ⚠️ PARTIALLY MET
**Expected:** Safety gates act as sequential filters on Herdr-ordered candidates. If no candidate passes, dispatcher reports "no candidate" — no fallback ranking.

**Actual:** When the Herdr list is empty (due to the stub), the dispatcher falls through to the legacy tier chain:
```
legacy tier chain: audit → implement → plan → idea (wl next --stage per tier)
```

This is a **second, competing ranking implementation** that re-ranks using a different order than the Herdr list. The code comments acknowledge this as "test-compat fallback" but it remains active in production.

**Evidence:**
- `downtime-worker.ts:2168-2200`: Fallthrough to legacy tier chain when `head.items.length === 0`
- Comments claim "Production `createDowntimeDeps` always returns a non-empty head" — this is false due to the stub

### AC3: Herdr list remains sole ranking path — ❌ FAILED
**Expected:** `fetchNextItems` / `selectWorkItems` / `regroupWorkItems` are the sole ranking path. No `wl next`/`database.ts` scoring change required.

**Actual:** The dispatcher still implements its own ranking via the legacy tier chain as a fallback. The Herdr list plumbing (`fetchNextItems` → `getHerdrListHead`) is not wired up in production.

### AC4: Contract documented — ✅ PASSED
**Expected:** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md` state explicitly: dispatcher selects the first dispatchable item from the Herdr selection list.

**Actual:** Documentation correctly states the contract. The issue is the implementation gap between documented intent and live code.

### AC5: No regression; observable agreement proven — ❌ FAILED
**Expected:** `wl next -n` / Herdr list / downtime pick agree; a reproducible sampling script shows agreement.

**Actual:** No agreement is possible because `getHerdrListHead` returns empty. The dispatcher picks from `wl next --stage plan_complete` (legacy) while the Herdr list shows a completely different order.

**Observable divergence on AI_Hell:**
- Herdr UI shows: 2 `plan_complete` items (1 `in_progress`), 4 `in_review` items
- Downtime dispatch picks: `wl next --stage plan_complete` → `AH-0MTG5MGPZ00986B4` (already in dispatched-marker)
- These do not agree

## Root Cause

The implementation landed in commit 5594bbb2 only the **dispatcher-side plumbing** (`dispatchFromHerdrList` with filters-only logic, `downtime-worker.ts:2137`). The **consumer-side wiring** (`getHerdrListHead` calling `fetchNextItems`) was intentionally stubbed as "production no-op" pending a fix to `WL-0MT26TE72002FLKX` (browseItemCount/cap/mandatory-merge fix).

This created an **incomplete wire-up**: the dispatcher calls `getHerdrListHead` expecting a populated list, but receives an empty array, and silently falls through to the legacy ranking.

## Impact

1. **Herdr extension and downtime dispatcher diverge on ranking** — exactly what AC1 was meant to prevent
2. **Downtime dispatch is effectively paused** for worklogs where the Herdr list would have candidates — e.g., `AI_Hell` shows items in Herdr UI but dispatcher picks from legacy tier (already-exhausted backlog)
3. **The stub comment is misleading** — "Production no-op for now" is a lie; it's always-on in production

## Recommended Resolution

1. **Immediate:** Replace the stub with a real `fetchNextItems` call, OR explicitly disable the dispatcher until the wire-up is complete
2. **Short-term:** Complete `WL-0MT26TE72002FLKX` (browseItemCount/cap/mandatory-merge fix) to unblock the Herdr list plumbing
3. **Medium-term:** Remove the legacy tier chain fallback from `downtime-worker.ts` once all tests use Herdr-head stubs
4. **Documentation:** Update AC4 docs to note the stub dependency and planned removal of legacy chain

## Items Requiring Attention

- `WL-0MT26TE72002FLKX` — "counts in Herdr selection list are incorrect" (open, intake_complete) — blocks the Herdr list plumbing
- `downtime-worker.ts:2168+` — Legacy tier chain fallback (should be removed, not retained)
- `index.ts:628` — Stub comment ("production no-op") is incorrect

## Ready to Close: No

# Intake Skill

## Invocation (canonical)

Resolve the skill directory via the **`skill_path` tool** (never the project
repo, which does not and must not contain copies of skill scripts):

```bash
python3 $(skill_path intake)/scripts/intake.py <work-item-id>
```

`$(skill_path <name>)` is the canonical runtime resolution for skill
locations (the `<name>/` folder under the global install at
`~/.pi/agent/skills`, or under this repo's `skill/` tree) — resolve it first
with the `skill_path` tool, then invoke the script with the **absolute**
path; never run `./scripts/...` relative to the project repo.

---

You are authoring a new Worklog work item for a feature or bug fix, following an interview-driven approach to gather requirements, constraints, Acceptance Criteria (synonym: Success Criteria), and related work — ensuring sufficient detail for a developer to complete the work.

## Inputs

- `$1` — The work-item-id (`<prefix>-<hash>`). If valid, fetch and use it; if missing/invalid, treat `$ARGUMENTS` as seed intent and create a new item as needed; if the user meant an existing item, ask for a valid id.
- `$ARGUMENTS` — Optional freeform arguments after `<work-item-id>`.

## Results and Outputs

- A 1–2 sentence headline summary of the intake brief; final brief text and the new or updated work item.
- Idempotence: rerunning `/skill:intake` reuses existing work items representing the same item.

## Hard requirements

- **Never copy skill scripts between repositories.** The intake scripts
  (and all skills) resolve their shared libraries from the canonical global
  skills location (`~/.pi/agent/skills`, per-skill via `$(skill_path <name>)`)
  or this repo's `skill/` tree. If a script reports a missing shared module
  (see the graceful-failure guard in
  [docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md](../../docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md#graceful-failure-for-missing-shared-modules)
  and `import_guard.py` at the skills root), reinstall via `scripts/install_pi.sh` or
  invoke the skill from its canonical location — do **not** copy/paste script
  files into another project, as real-copy installs without `shared/` break
  import resolution.

- Do not create a work item for this intake process itself.
- Interview style: concise, high-signal questions, max three per round.
- Do not invent requirements — ask the user; don't ask leading or unnecessary questions when an obvious answer exists.
- If a response is unclear or ambiguous, ask for clarification rather than guessing.
- Respect `.gitignore` and agent framework ignore rules; prefer short multiple-choice suggestions but allow freeform.
- All work-item descriptions and comments **must be written in Markdown**.
- The goal is sufficient detail for a clear work item — not an exhaustive spec.
- Do not include procedural next steps (e.g., \"Proceed to planning\") in the brief; progression is handled by stage transitions.

## Status Lifecycle

All status transitions are managed by the shared `StatusLifecycle` context manager (from `../shared/status_lifecycle.py`) — never ad-hoc `wl update --status` commands. The lifecycle script at `$(skill_path intake)/scripts/intake.py` is the canonical CLI:

- **Claim** (before any other step): `python3 $(skill_path intake)/scripts/intake.py start <work-item-id> --assignee \"<AGENT>\"` — sets `status=in_progress`, prevents concurrent claims.
- **Auto-complete** (skip full intake for sufficiently defined items): `python3 $(skill_path intake)/scripts/intake.py auto-complete <work-item-id>`.
- **Finish**: `python3 $(skill_path intake)/scripts/intake.py finish <work-item-id> [--description-file <path>]`.
- **Abort** (release on failure): `python3 $(skill_path intake)/scripts/intake.py abort <work-item-id>`.

Guard with `StatusLifecycle.require_claimed(<id>)` before any mutation; on in-session resume after producer approval, re-claim first via `StatusLifecycle.ensure_claimed(<id>)` (idempotent). ## Worklog resolution

`intake.py` routes every `wl` call through the shared `run_wl` helper, which injects `--worklog-dir` with precedence: (1) explicit `--worklog-dir`, (2) prefix-to-sibling scan (item-id prefix → sibling projects' worklog stores), (3) cwd chain (`<cwd>/.worklog`, git root, nearest ancestor), (4) no flag — `wl` resolves from cwd. Full detail: [docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md](../../docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md) and `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`.

## Process (must follow)

### 0. Claim the work item

- **Before any other step**, claim the work item:
  ```bash
  python3 $(skill_path intake)/scripts/intake.py start <work-item-id> --assignee Map
  ```
  This must happen before any evaluation, context gathering, or preflight checks.

### 0b. Per-child intake pass (when children exist)

If the work item already has children, run intake on each child before proceeding:

- Run `wl show <work-item-id> --children --json` to fetch existing children.
- Order children by dependency edges using `wl dep list <id> --json` (topological order, ties broken by listed order).
- For each child, run the intake process on it (steps 1–11, recursing if the child has its own children).
- Use the shared tree-coverage helper to verify AC coverage across existing children:
  ```python
  from skill.shared.tree_coverage import run_coverage_review
  review = run_coverage_review(<work-item-id>)
  ```
- If the coverage review returns `recommendation: \"stop\"` with unresolvable conflicts,
  record the conflicts as a comment and stop — leave the item `open`.
- If the coverage review returns `recommendation: \"auto_close\"`, apply the auto-closed gaps
  and note them in a comment.
- If the coverage review returns `recommendation: \"proceed\"`, continue to Step 1.
- Idempotence: re-running must not create duplicate children or duplicate comments.

### 1. Evaluate whether intake is required (agent responsibility)

Run a lightweight evaluation to decide whether the item is well-defined enough to skip the interview/draft. Conservative, idempotent heuristics: `stage` already `intake_complete` or later → skip; description has a clear one-line headline + an \"## Acceptance Criteria\" section (1–3 measurable bullets) + concise implementation notes (≤~200 words) → well-defined; small item (`task`/`bug`, not `epic`) with explicit ACs + minimal implementation sketch → prefer to complete; parent/child relationships already express the context → consider skipping.

If intake is not needed:

```bash
python3 $(skill_path intake)/scripts/intake.py auto-complete <work-item-id>
wl comment add <work-item-id> \"Intake auto-complete: work item appears sufficiently defined (ACs present / small task).\" --actor Map --json   # optional
```

If uncertain, fall back to the normal intake process (no auto-complete on borderline evidence).

### 2. Gather context (agent responsibility)

- Derive 2–6 keywords from `<seed-context>` and user input; search work items (`wl search <keywords> --json`) and the repo (ignore `node_modules`, `.git`, `.`-prefixed folders).
- Duplicates: highlight and ask if they represent the work; if confirmed, ask the user to resolve; if parent/child, create the relationship when creating work items.
- Output labelled lists — \"Potentially related docs\" (paths) and \"Potentially related work items\" (titles + IDs) — and summarize each.

### 3. Work Item prep (agent responsibility)

- If `<work-item-id>` was provided: review `issueType`; update if it doesn't match: `wl update <work-item-id> --issue-type <correct-type> --json`.
- If no id was provided: extract a working title, infer the issue type (guide below), and create:
  ```bash
  wl create --stage idea --status in_progress --title \"<title>\" --description \"<seed-context>\" --issue-type <type> --assignee Map --json
  ```
  (Creation is not a status transition — the initial status is set at creation.) Remember the returned id.

**Issue type decision guide** — full table in [docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md](../../docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md). Summary:

- `bug` — currently **incorrect/broken**; the change corrects wrong behavior (not net-new capability).
- `feature` — **adds new capability** that did not exist before (not merely fixing broken).
- `chore` — **does not change code behavior** (config, CI, docs, deps, formatting).
- `task` — general-purpose (tests, refactoring, investigation, benchmarking).
- `epic` — **large scope** needing decomposition into subtasks.

**Decision procedure** — when uncertain, ask: (1) *broken/incorrect?* → `bug`; (2) *net-new behavior?* → `feature`; (3) *no code-behavior change (docs/CI/deps/formatting)?* → `chore`; (4) *general-purpose (tests/refactoring/investigation)?* → `task`; (5) *large enough for subtasks?* → `epic`.

**Priority classification guide** — use these rules to assign the correct `priority` (consulted only when the operator has not supplied an explicit priority value via `--priority` or similar flag):

| Priority  | Use when… | Do NOT use when… | Examples |
|-----------|-----------|-------------------|----------|
| `critical` | Security vulnerabilities, data loss, broken builds, or blocking the release pipeline | The issue is not blocking or does not involve data security/integrity | Patching a CVE, fixing CI pipeline failure, recovering from data corruption |
| `high`    | Major features, important bugs, or anything blocking other work | The work is not urgent or blocking | Shipping a major feature, fixing a significant user-facing bug |
| `medium`  | Default priority for standard features, enhancements, or non-blocking bugs | The issue is critical/high urgency or trivial | Regular feature development, minor bug fixes, improvements |
| `low`     | Polish, minor optimizations, nice-to-have improvements | The issue affects functionality or user experience | Cosmetic fixes, minor refactoring, documentation polish |

**Decision procedure** — when priority is not specified by the operator, ask:
1. *Does this involve security, data loss, or a broken build/release pipeline?* → `critical`
2. *Is this a major feature, important bug, or is it blocking other work?* → `high`
3. *Is this trivial polish or a nice-to-have with no functional impact?* → `low`
4. *Otherwise?* → `medium` (default for standard work)

> **Precedence rule:** Operator-specified priority (via `--priority` flag or explicit directive) always takes absolute precedence over classification. Classification is a fallback only.

### 4. Interview

Skip if the seed context suffices to draft a clear brief. Otherwise: soft limit of 3 questions per round (1+ rounds); do NOT ask questions answerable by repo search — use gathered context; goal is enough understanding to draft a problem definition with user stories, ACs, and related work (not a complete spec); if ambiguous, ask for clarification rather than guessing; do not proceed until sufficient information is gathered.

**Producer review:** When the agent cannot proceed without producer input (clarifying questions unanswered, critical information missing), mark the work item as needing producer review:

```bash
wl reviewed <work-item-id> true
```

This flags the item so the producer knows attention is required. The agent should STOP and wait for the producer's response. Once answers are received, continue the interview or proceed.

### 5. Draft intake brief (agent responsibility)

- Write a brief to `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-<title>-<work-item-id>.md` with: **Problem statement** (1–2 sentences), **Users** (with example user stories), **Acceptance Criteria** (3–5 measurable bullets), **Constraints**, **Existing state**, **Desired change**, **Key Files (predicted)** (published as a `**Key Files:**` section; e.g. ``- `path/to/file.py` — Needs new function for X feature``), **Related work**.
- Present the draft and invite feedback; incorporate edits but don't block for approval — proceed automatically to the review stages.

### 6. Five mini-review stages (agent responsibility; must follow)

Run five conservative review iterations on the draft brief. If a proposed change could alter intent, ask a clarifying question first. After each stage: \"Finished <type> review: <changes>\" or \"Finished <type> review: no changes needed\".

1. **Completeness** — Problem, ACs, Constraints present and actionable; add missing bullets or concise placeholders when obvious.
2. **Capture fidelity** — User answers accurately/neutrally represented; shorten only for clarity.
3. **Related-work & traceability** — Related docs/work items correctly referenced.
4. **Risks & assumptions** — Add missing risks, mitigations, failure modes, assumptions in short bullets; include a scope-creep risk (record extra opportunities as linked work items, not scope).
5. **Polish & handoff** — Tighten language, copy-paste-ready commands, final 1–2 sentence headline.

### 7. Call the find_related skill

Collect related work via `/skill:find-related <work-item-id>`; add a report to the work item description.

### 8. Review the new issue in project context

- Adding dependencies: `wl comment add <work-item-id> --comment \"Blocks:<blocked-id>\" --json` / `wl comment add <work-item-id> --comment \"Blocked-by:<blocking-id>\" --json`
- Adjusting priority: `wl update <work-item-id> --priority <level> --json`

### 9. Update the work item and verify coverage

Write the final draft to the work item description:

```bash
python3 $(skill_path intake)/scripts/intake.py finish <work-item-id> --description-file .worklog/tmp/intake-draft-<title>-<work-item-id>.md
```

**AC coverage verification:** After updating the description, run the AC coverage review:

```python
from skill.shared.tree_coverage import run_coverage_review
review = run_coverage_review(<work-item-id>)
```

- If ``recommendation == \"proceed\"`` or ``\"auto_close\"`` → mark `intake_complete`.
- If ``recommendation == \"stop\"`` → **do NOT advance the stage**. Leave the item `open` with a comment describing the conflicts.

Then advance the stage:

This transitions `status=open`, `stage=intake_complete`.

### 10. Calculate Effort and Risk (agent responsibility; must follow)

- Call the effort_and_risk skill on the new or updated work item:
  ```bash
  python3 $(skill_path effort-and-risk)/scripts/orchestrate_estimate.py <work-item-id>
  ```
  (Refer to `../effort-and-risk/SKILL.md` for details.)

### 11. Finishing (must do as the final step only)

- `wl sync` to sync changes.  > **Note:** on a repo with **no commits yet** `wl sync` fails (unborn HEAD) — create an initial commit (`git commit --allow-empty -m \"chore: initial\"`) or use `wl sync --no-push`. See `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`.
- `wl show <work-item-id>` (not --json); remove temp files (`.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-<title>-<work-item-id>.md`).
- Output a structured summary (`# Objective` headline, `# Acceptance Criteria` list, `# Effort and Risk` sizing; full template in [docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md](../../docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md)). The AC list always includes: at least one testing/validation criterion; \"All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.\"; and \"Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.\"  > **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline. Do not include CI/CD pipeline tests.
- Finish with \"This completes the Intake process for <work-item-id> <work-item-title>\"

### 12. Error/abort handling

If the intake process fails or is interrupted before completion:

```bash
python3 $(skill_path intake)/scripts/intake.py abort <work-item-id>
```

This resets `status=open`, releasing the item for other agents.

## Traceability & idempotence

- All work item updates or creations must be idempotent: rerunning `/skill:intake` must not create duplicate links or clarifying-question entries.

## Editing rules & safety

- Preserve author intent; if uncertain, add a clarifying question instead of assuming.
- Keep edits minimal and conservative. Respect `.gitignore` and other ignore rules when searching the repo.
- If any automated step fails or is ambiguous, surface an explicit Open Question and pause for guidance.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (must include)

Every interview-driven intake must produce an auditable Appendix of clarifying questions asked and answers provided. Append it to the final draft file AND include it in the work item description (`wl update --description-file`).

Per entry: question text as asked; answer, answering party, and evidence/link (id, path, PR); prior answers if changed + final accepted answer; research summary (1–6 sentences) with links when applicable.

Example:

- Q: \"Who is the primary user?\" — Answer (user@acme): \"Internal support engineers\". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: \"Can we reuse service X?\" — Answer (engineer@acme): \"Partially; need a small wrapper. Research: inspected services/x, no adapter — created follow-up wl-789\".

Behavior: append before final approval; **idempotent** (update existing records, never duplicate); mark open questions \"OPEN QUESTION\" with context; respect `.gitignore`. Privacy: record only user/authorized-stakeholder info; redact secrets with a note (\"[REDACTED sensitive snippet]\"). Traceability: each entry linkable; include `related-to:<work-item-id>` or file-path references when practical.


## Final step: standardized end-of-session report

Render the canonical end-of-session report (helper: [`../report/SKILL.md`](../report/SKILL.md)) as the **last step**, replacing any ad-hoc end-of-session summary:

```bash
  [--notes \"<freeform context/caveats/assumptions>\"] \
  [--next-action <review|plan|implement|...>]
```

The script prints the rendered report to stdout — **paste it verbatim into

      \"description\": \"# RCA: near-zero downtime dispatches overnight Sep 8→9 (ContextHub 0, TCE 3) and dispatcher design gaps

> **Revised 2026-09-09** — the ContextHub root cause is now identified precisely (sprint-complete auto-disable, below). Earlier draft blamed worker liveness; that was wrong.

## Problem statement

Overnight (cheap window ≈22:00Z Sep 8 → 07:00Z Sep 9) the machine-wide downtime dispatcher produced **3 dispatches, all Tableau-Card-Engine** (TCE), and **zero for ContextHub** — ContextHub's typical night is 9–13, TCE 4–8 (rolling `downtime-dispatches.log` counts, prior nights Sep 3–8). The producer asked: (a) why so few, (b) why open_source_llm and AI_Hell did not dispatch, (c) whether TCE was capacity-limited or missed items, and (d) how to make the dispatcher reliable overnight — specifically whether the review-queue-depth gate stops *all* work and whether audits of `in_review` items should still run while the queue is deep.

## Evidence & per-project timeline

Per-project check-in density in `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` (rolling, instance id per project):

| Project | Worker overnight | Offers | Dispatches (cheap window) | Cause |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ContextHub (`4b3fbc4d`) | **HALTED 21:53Z→07:11Z** (no check-in log lines at all) | none possible | **0** | **Sprint-complete auto-disable tripped**: root-only `completed/in_review` count crossed the `browseItemCount` threshold (default 20) at ≈21:34Z when the Sep 8 colour-code/audit batch completed into `in_review`; tick() then early-returns BEFORE the leader-election/check-in block, so no check-ins are logged and nothing dispatches. Count fell back to 19 (root-only) by morning → marker cleared → resumed 07:11Z. See Root cause A. |
| Tableau-Card-Engine (`8a1c2221`) | UP all night (15 check-ins/h, 4-min leader cadence; root-only in_review 11 < 20) | only 06:36–07:10Z (CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128, then CG-0MSTOATDU006UGAX) | **3** (plan CG-0MTT0K9RX 22:54Z, implement CG-0MTT0K9RX 00:08Z, implement CG-0MTSHG8RP 06:37Z) | One-pane-at-a-time capacity (each implement occupies the local slot for 2+ h — the 06:37 pane was still running at 08:20Z) AND head-window starvation (Root cause B) |
| AI_Hell (`00c96094`) | UP all night (12/h; root-only in_review 13 < 20) | all `null` | 0 | Head wall: 0 open items; its `in_review` items needing audit are **blocked by stale audit dispatch-markers** (Root cause D: AH-0MTFOSOHN001Q620, AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40, AH-0MTG5MGPZ00986B4 were audited Aug 31/Sep 2, later changed so their audits are stale, `npr=false` — but their old audit markers permanently exclude them), the rest are `npr=true` or audit-marked. Also one item stuck in-progress (Root cause E). |
| open_source_llm (`253b3527`) | UP all night (12/h; root-only in_review 10 < 20) | all `null` | 0 | Head wall + dead zones: 83 open items but the Herdr head (24 visible) is 100% non-dispatchable — items stranded on the retired `in_progress` stage, `plan_complete` items with **no risk/effort** (6 of 7 open plan_complete items, incl. OSL-0MSG7XUY0009OTVA — fails implement caps fail-closed, Root cause C), npr-flagged items, audit-marked items; dispatchable ruff/intake backlog ranks below the fetch window (Root cause B). Earlier Sep 6: repeated 3-strike `wl-error` pauses from the pre-fix cross-root bug (WL-0MTQ14W7L003II5A, fixed Sep 7) |

## Root causes

- **A. Sprint-complete auto-disable halts ALL dispatch (incl. audits + check-ins) when the review queue crosses `browseItemCount`.** `createDowntimeWorker.tick()` (downtime-worker.ts ~3110) counts root-only `completed/in_review` items (`fetchCompletedItemCount` = `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only`); when the count ≥ `browseItemCount` (default 20) it writes `.herdr-downtime-disabled` (per worklog root) and every subsequent tick **early-returns before the leader-election/check-in block** → no coordination log entries (the 21:53Z silence), no dispatch. It removes the marker only when the count falls below 20 (resume 07:11Z at 19). This is the direct answer to \"did ContextHub stop because in_review > browse count\": **yes** — via this auto-disable, which stops audits and plan/intake too, exactly the opposite of the producer's intended policy (keep auditing a deep review queue; only hold NEW non-critical implement). It is a *different* mechanism from the review-queue-depth gate (WL-0MT2UQWOR007CYY9, finding B2), which is dead-on-production.
- **B. Head-window starvation.** The dispatch/offer decision scans only `getHerdrListHead` = `fetchNextItems(30)` (index.ts), windowed by `browseItemCount` for non-mandatory items (OSL returned 24). When the top ~30 ranked items are a wall of non-dispatchable entries — in-progress claims, `needsProducerReview=true`, fresh-audited `in_review`, dispatched-marker exclusions, above-caps/no-risk-effort items — dispatchable work behind the wall is **invisible**, `computeMostImportantItem` returns `noCandidate`, and `runCoordinationCheckIn` **removes the own entry**. - **B2. The review-queue-depth gate (WL-0MT2UQWOR007CYY9) is effectively dead on the production path.** The gate (`reviewQueueCount ≥ browseItemCount` → skip non-critical implement) exists only in the **legacy tier chain** (~2497–2541), production-unreachable when the Herdr head is non-empty. `dispatchFromHerdrList`, `computeMostImportantItem` and `dispatchFromCoordination` never read it. - **C. Items missing risk/effort are silently stranded at the implement gate.** `classifyItemForDispatch` fails closed on absent risk/effort (`riskOrdinal(null)`/`effortOrdinal(null)` → null). OSL has 6 of 7 open `plan_complete` items with no risk/effort (OSL-0MSG7XUY0009OTVA etc.) — permanently invisible to implement dispatch with no reason surfaced. No mechanism evaluates risk/effort for them, and the implement skill refuses to run without the gate values.
- **D. Stale audit dispatch-markers permanently strand audit-needing `in_review` items.** The audit marker exclusion in the Herdr-head path uses `auditDispatchedItemIds` = **all** `kind=audit` markers in the 100-entry rolling log — **no staleness window** (unlike the 2 h active-audit single-flight). AI_Hell trio: AH-0MTFOSOHN001Q620 / AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40 (audited Sep 2, items changed afterwards → audits now stale, `npr=false`) and AH-0MTG5MGPZ00986B4 (audited Aug 31, changed Sep 6) — all audit-eligible by freshness but excluded by 6–7-day-old markers. No timeout/no-activity detection exists for in-progress claims (relates to hydrator epic WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI).
- **F. Deployment/runtime heterogeneity + no per-tick diagnostics.** TCE ran machine-dir coordination; ContextHub's offers never reached the machine file; only outcomes are logged, never \"why no candidate\" per tick — the 01:00–06:00Z TCE null stretch and OSL's all-night nulls are unreconstructible post-hoc (capacity vs missed items cannot be separated without P5 diagnostics).

1. **\"When in_review > browseItemCount do we actively stop ALL dispatch?\"** — Effectively yes for ContextHub, but via the **sprint-complete auto-disable** (root cause A), not the review-queue-depth gate. The gate itself (WL-0MT2UQWOR007CYY9) is not wired to the production path at all (B2). The auto-disable stops audits and plan/intake too, and even suppresses coordination check-in logging.
2. **\"Shouldn't we permit audit of in_review items while the queue is deep?\"** — Yes. Audits are the queue drain and are never depth-gated by design; the auto-disable defeats that. - **P1 — Worker supervision + overnight liveness tripwire.** The downtime tick is a scheduler task inside the worklist pane (`worklist.ts` `scheduler.addTask({ id:'downtime' … })` — \"runs while the worklist pane is open\"). data.author: Map
data.comment:
Manual smoke checklist — typing gate (WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH, implemented c4b02c26, docs WL-0MTVALTA000445RM)

Goal: confirm background sync/refresh stops while a text-input overlay is open and resumes after close.

Prerequisites
- Worklist pane open with defaults (`autoSync=true` / `syncIntervalMs=60000`, `autoRefresh=true` / `refreshIntervalMs=30000`).
- A terminal window to run the process checks below.

Steps
1. Sync suppressed while typing
   - Open a text-input overlay (command-parameter form via its chord, or Ship It \`S\`).
   - Hold it open for >= 2x syncIntervalMs (>= 120s).
   - Run: `ps -eo args | grep -E 'wl sync' | grep -v grep`
   - Expected: no `wl sync` spawns attributable to this pane (tick skipped). Header/list is unchanged while the overlay is open.
2. Refresh/re-render suppressed while typing
   - Same overlay, hold open for >= 2x refreshIntervalMs (>= 60s).
   - Expected: no list re-render, no flicker/focus loss; the typed text is preserved character-for-character.
3. No dropped keystrokes across a scheduled tick
   - With the overlay open, type a long string rapidly so keystrokes land across a tick boundary.
   - Expected: the typed string matches exactly what was entered — zero dropped characters. Repeat for the Ship It dialog and for note editing (md-note-edit opens a FormState, so it shares the same guard).
4. Resume after close
   - Close the overlay (Esc/Enter as appropriate).
   - Expected: the next regular tick (<= 30s refresh / <= 60s sync) fires normally. No immediate queued refresh is required or emitted — skip, don't coalesce.
5. Regression guard (not typing)
   - With no overlay open, confirm the normal 30s refresh and 60s sync cadence continues, and the pause-when-hidden / heartbeat / DB-change gates still behave as before.

Notes
- Downtime and mode-switch worker ticks are intentionally NOT gated: they never re-render the list while a modal is open; audit recorded in code comments in worklist.ts.
- Automated coverage: worklist.test.ts (isInputActive unit + scheduler integration + note-edit coverage) green in the full suite.

data.author: pi
data.comment:
Root cause (diagnosed, not a product regression): `isPaneVisible()` resolves the herdr binary as `process.env.HERDR_BIN_PATH ?? "herdr"` (visibility.ts). The test exec mock in `worklist-visibility.test.ts` only recognises `bin === "herdr"` (makeExecMock), but when the suite runs INSIDE a herdr pane the inherited `HERDR_BIN_PATH` (e.g. `/home/rgardler/.local/bin/herdr`) is used, so the mock falls through to its generic branch, `payload.result.tab.focused` is undefined, and `isPaneVisible()` fails open to `true` → the "hidden" refresh tick dispatches the fetcher. Because `afterEach` deletes `HERDR_BIN_PATH`, only the FIRST test in the file is affected — exactly the observed 1 failed / 16 passed. CI (no herdr env) is green, so this is a test-hermeticity defect, not a regression on dev.

Scope: make the test hermetic — clear inherited herdr env vars in `beforeEach` and make the exec mock match `herdr tab get` by ARGUMENTS rather than the exact binary name. No production-code change.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
## Root cause identified and fixed

The intermittent 'error (?)' icon was NOT an unknown-stage fallback. The lines showing '�' are the U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER produced when the line-truncation loops in formatItemLine and truncateLine appended only the LOW surrogate of a supplementary-plane emoji (u+1F513, u+1F4CB, u+1F50D, ...). Writing that unpaired surrogate to stdout encodes it as EF BF BD, which terminals render as a white diamond/question-mark glyph. The bug is intermittent because it only fires when a row's line width exceeds the pane AND the truncation point lands inside an emoji (narrow pane / long title).

Fixed in packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts (both truncation loops now append the full character — both surrogate halves — and advance by two code units). Regression tests added in packages/herdr/src/worklist-icon-truncation.test.ts asserting no lone surrogates / no U+FFFD after UTF-8 round-tripping for formatItemLine, formatMetadataPanel and formatDetailContent across truncating widths, including the exact reported row (WL-0MU55UDBJ008DJ67 shape: status open + stage plan_complete + critical + long title).

Verification: full suite green at the committed state (85 files / 641 tests passed, 4 skipped; second suite 20 files / 415 passed; 0 failures). Commit 6af00da2 pushed to dev.
